title: Interpretable Meta-Policies for Neural Decision Making
abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning remains difficult to interpret and align due to the black-box nature of neural networks. While (neuro-)symbolic approaches improve transparency by incorporating symbolic reasoning, applying them directly to low-level actions results in overly complex, unreadable policies. We introduce NEXUS, a hierarchical RL framework that resolves this tension by combining neural skills with symbolic meta-policies. By shifting transparent reasoning to high-level skills rather than atomic actions, NEXUS drastically reduces symbolic complexity without sacrificing environment performance. Object-centric observations enable high-level reasoning and the design of reward functions and meta-policies by interaction with LLMs. We demonstrate that NEXUS agents learn disentangled skills, are interpretable regarding high-level goals, are better aligned to goals described in the game manual, less prone to reward hacking and more robust to game simplifications than deep RL. Finally, we isolate and evaluate the impact of different meta-policy architectures (neural, symbolic, neuro-symbolic) on environmental return and aligned task performance.

title: Graph Representation Learning via Adaptive Expectile Aggregation
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) rely critically on neighborhood aggregation, yet conventional mean aggregation may fail to capture class-relevant distributional information, particularly in heterophilic graphs. We propose ExpectileGCN, an adaptive graph aggregation framework that introduces a learnable expectile level to capture neighborhood information beyond the mean. The proposed operator continuously adjusts aggregation between minimum- and maximum-type behaviors, with mean aggregation as a special case. A differentiable approximation based on sigmoid smoothing and fixed-point iterations enables end-to-end optimization. Theoretically, we establish stability properties and transductive generalization guarantees for ExpectileGCN. We further investigate its classification risk under heterophilic neighborhood models. For informative neighborhoods, we show that expectile aggregation can exploit class-dependent scale differences to achieve a classification advantage over mean aggregation. Under a local asymptotic regime with diminishing per-neighbor label informativeness, we establish that this advantage can persist in terms of limiting classification risk. Experiments on homophilic and heterophilic benchmark graphs demonstrate strong predictive performance and improved robustness under feature corruption and structural perturbations.

title: Can Complementary Signals Bridge Similarity Islands? Manifold-Augmented Graph Embedding for Multimodal Recommendation
abstract: Multimodal Recommender Systems (MMRS) leverage rich item features to mitigate data sparsity, yet similarity-driven graph construction and propagation can favor semantically similar substitutes over functionally related complements. When behavioral associations connect semantically distant items, complementary signals can remain geometrically isolated, yielding fragmented "Similarity Islands" and semantic drift when standard propagation is applied. To overcome these limitations, we propose MAGE (Manifold-Augmented Graph Embedding), a framework for personalized multimodal ranking that decouples complementarity modeling into offline geometric warping and online topological propagation. The offline phase enhances item representations by extracting complement-aware residual directions via a Soft Conceptor mechanism and injecting them under a local gap-preserving constraint, incorporating co-purchase evidence while controlling the magnitude of geometric perturbation. Synergistically, the online phase employs an asymmetric dual-stream GNN that treats visual features as stable anchors and augmented textual features as flexible probes, fused through a self-calibrated cross-modal mechanism to reconcile shared semantics and modality-specific residual cues. Extensive experiments on four Amazon datasets show that MAGE yields consistent improvements over strong multimodal recommendation baselines. Together with the supporting analyses in the appendix, these results suggest that geometry-aware augmentation can alleviate the semantic mismatch that arises in complementary recommendation settings. Our code is available at https://github.com/Alex-bupt/mage.

title: Test-Time Communication in Trading Agent Swarms
abstract: Communication between agents has mostly been studied on tasks with a shared objective and fast, clear feedback. Trading has neither: each agent manages its own account, with decisions being scored by markets late and noisily. A trading swarm is thus a population of independent decision-makers rather than a team, for which convergence is a risk and not the goal. We ran 200 agents from four model families in groups of ten under five communication regimes, from isolation to message boards and shared notes, over seven US trading days (1 to 9 October 2026), logging everything each agent read before every decision. In two of the four families, communicating groups came to hold far more of the same stocks than the isolated group. A group's return was largely the return on what its members held in common. Seeing a post from a groupmate made an agent 7 percentage points more likely to reuse an eight-word phrase from it. Agents that started too close together to see each other's posts shared such a phrase in 14% of cases, the rate that common inputs produce. Seeing the post did not detectably change that morning's trades. Case studies traced the adoption of positions and decision rules over subsequent days, and communicating groups sold in step more often than isolated ones. Because isolated groups also converged on the same stocks, sometimes completely, assessments of herding need to measure excess convergence relative to a no-peer baseline.

Agents that started too close together to see each other's posts shared such a phrase in 14% of cases, the rate that common inputs produce. Seeing the post did not detectably change that morning's trades. Case studies traced the adoption of positions and decision rules over subsequent days, and communicating groups sold in step more often than isolated ones. Because isolated groups also converged on the same stocks, sometimes completely, assessments of herding need to measure excess convergence relative to a no-peer baseline.

title: A Domain-Separated Multi-Agent RAG Architecture for University Academic Q&A
abstract: 대학 학사 Q&A는 장학금·학칙·교과과정 등 이질적 다중 도메인의 복합체로, 단일 RAG 파이 프라인으로는 도메인 간 검색 간섭과 답변 커버리지 부족이 발생한다. 본 논문은 도메인별 분리 인덱스, 하이브리드 라우팅, 그룹 집중도 기반 문서 확장(Retrieve-then-Expand), 경량 검증을 통합한 멀티 에이전트 RAG 시스템을 제안한다. 10,745건의 학사 데이터와 300개 질문 벤치마크, 골든 라벨을 구축하여 검색 정확도를 측정하였다. 제안 시스템은 100개 층화표본에서 Routed-domain Purity 1.000을 기록하여 호출 도메인 외 문서의 혼입을 구조적으로 차단하였으며, Multi-agent Recall 0.895로 복합 질의에 필요한 에이전트를 높은 비율로 호출하였다. 검색 정밀도는 gold-entity 기반 대리 지표에서 단일 인덱스 대비 개선됨을 별도로 확인하였다. 블라인드 인간 평가에서 완전성(+0.83, p < 0.001)과 유용성(+0.67, p < 0.001)의 실질적 개선을 확인하였다.

title: ETAMem: Decoupling and Aligning Heterogeneous Memory for Long-Term Conversational Agents
abstract: Long-term memory enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to maintain coherent and personalized interactions across extended conversations. However, existing memory systems face two key challenges: (1) Information Entanglement, where heterogeneous information is mixed within coarse-grained memory units; and (2) Organizational Mismatch, where memory structures based primarily on semantic similarity may overlook other associations. To address these challenges, we propose ETAMem, a multi-view memory framework that decouples heterogeneous conversational information and aligns memory representations and organization with its distinct characteristics. Specifically, heterogeneous information parsing extracts atomic memory units and identifies affective information. View-specific memory structuring then organizes these units into three complementary hierarchical views: Event, Affect, and Time. ETAMem incrementally maintains memory structures with adaptively calibrated thresholds. For retrieval, entropy-based retrieval allocates query-specific budgets across views and performs hierarchical search within each view. Experiments on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S demonstrate that ETAMem outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving relative accuracy improvements of 12.46% and 7.96%, respectively, while maintaining competitive token efficiency. Further analyses demonstrate the complementary benefits of different memory views.

title: Iterative Reasoning Framework for Large Language Models via Meta-Level Feedback
abstract: 대형 언어 모델(LLM)은 복잡한 추론 과제에서 우수한 성능을 보이며, 이를 향상시키기 위한 다양한 기법이 제안되어 왔다. Chain-of-Thought는 중간 추론 단계를 통해 다중홉 추론을 유도하지만, 단일 경로의 오류 전파 한계를 가진다. Self-Consistency는 다양한 추론 경로를 생성하여 이를 완화하지만 높은 비용을 요구한다. GPT-4o, GPT-5와 같은 상용 LLM은 향상된 추론 성능에도 불구하고, 추론 과정이 주로 모델 내부에서 수행되어 이를 직접 관찰하거나 해석하기 어렵다. 본 연구는 이러한 한계를 보완하기 위해 하나의 LLM을 메타 세션과 실행 세션으로 분리한 단계적 추론 프레임워크를 제안한다. 메타 세션은 추론 상태를 점검하고 다음 단계의 목표와 방향을 결정하며, 실행 세션은 이에 따라 추론을 수행한다. 이러한 설계를 통해 추론의 안정성, 관리 가능성 및 설명 가능성을 향상시키며, 다중홉 및 인과 추론 과제에서 기존 기법 대비 우수한 성능을 달성하였다.

title: CRISP: Co-designing Pruning and Scheduling for Efficient MoE Inference on Edge Servers
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference on memory-constrained edge platforms is often dominated by expert-weight movement rather than computation. Although each token activates only a small subset of experts, routing is input-dependent, so all experts must remain accessible and memory movement dominates latency. Existing approaches such as uniform pruning and expert dropping overlook two properties of MoE execution: expert combinations are highly skewed in frequency, and experts contribute asymmetrically within each combination. We present CRISP, a combination-aware framework that co-designs pruning and runtime scheduling for efficient MoE serving on memory-constrained edge platforms. CRISP reorders neurons by importance so one stored expert can support multiple execution widths, assigns differentiated execution to hot, warm, and cold combinations based on frequency and expert role, and exploits heterogeneous widths to overlap expert loading with computation. Across Mixtral-8x7B and DeepSeek-MoE-16B, CRISP improves throughput by up to $2.1\times$ at the same memory budget while limiting accuracy loss to 3.6\% relative to full-width inference. Our results highlight that efficient edge MoE serving requires jointly optimizing which expert capacity is preserved and how expert execution is scheduled.

title: Ingegneria della Conoscenza e Linked Open Data per il Superamento del Paradigma Isolazionista della Sardegna Antica: L'Architettura dell'Ipergrafo Semantico della Rotta Aristeica
abstract: Autore: Luigi Usai Ruolo: Ricercatore Indipendente & Knowledge Engineer ORCID: 0009-0003-3001-717X Data di Completamento: 27 Ottobre 2026 Repository e Dataset FAIR: Progetto Rotta Aristeica (RDF Turtle, JSON-LD, NDJSON, WebGIS) Licenza: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) Abstract (Italiano) Per oltre un secolo la storiografia e l'archeologia tradizionale hanno interpretato la Sardegna protostorica secondo un paradigma isolazionista, descrivendo l'isola come una realtà geografica passiva, marginale e chiusa nei propri rilievi montuosi, subalterna alle colonizzazioni esterne. Tuttavia, le recenti evidenze archeometriche (isotopi del piombo, diffusione transmarina dei lingotti oxhide, metallurgia nuragica attestata a Creta, Lipari, Cannatello e Huelva), paleogenomiche (aDNA) e toponomastiche dimostrano che il bacino tirrenico costituiva un polo marittimo e pirotecnologico attivo, strettamente integrato nei circuiti commerciali del Mediterraneo centro-occidentale e nordafricano. Il presente contributo propone un modello metodologico computazionale fondato sull'Ingegneria della Conoscenza e sui Linked Open Data (LOD) per strutturare, interrogare e validare in modo riproducibile questa complessa rete di evidenze storiche ed etno-archeologiche. Viene presentata l'architettura dell'ipergrafo semantico del progetto Rotta Aristeica, una base di conoscenza aperta conforme ai principi FAIR che integra oltre 5.120 record ontologici (modellati secondo standard W3C, CIDOC-CRM, Schema.org e DCAT-AP_IT), 804 marker cartografici geodetici privi di dipendenze proprietarie e 939 asserzioni scientifiche verificate. Elemento cardine del modello è l'introduzione del Pattern di Biforcazione a Doppio Iperarco Concorrente (Dual Hyperedge Architecture), che attua formalmente il principio di demarcazione popperiana distinguendo nettamente l'Iperarco del Consenso Accademico Ufficiale (VerifiedAcademicConsensus) dalle ipotesi speculative di lavoro (SpeculativeHypothesis). Vengono infine presentati due casi studio applicativi: 1) la mappatura della koinè toponomastica emporica tra la Sardegna e il Nord Africa (il caso di MQM ḤDŠ / Macomades a Magomadas e nella Byzacena punica); 2) il rilevamento algoritmico e filologico di refusi cartografici storici nelle basi di conoscenza aperte collaborative (la correzione del toponimo Panido per Pactya nell'istmo del Chersoneso Tracico). Parole Chiave: Ingegneria della Conoscenza, Linked Open Data (LOD), Ipergrafo Semantico, Sardegna Nuragica, Facies Sarda, Fenicio-Punico, Demarcazione Popperiana, Digital Humanities, Archeometria. Abstract (English) For over a century, traditional historiography and archaeology have approached protohistoric Sardinia through an isolationist paradigm, depicting the island as a passive, peripheral territory shielded by its mountain ranges and vulnerable to external colonization. Nevertheless, state-of-the-art archaeometric analyses (lead isotope provenance, trans-Mediterranean dispersal of oxhide ingots, Nuragic metallurgy documented in Crete, Lipari, Cannatello, and Huelva), paleogenomics (aDNA), and semitic toponomastics demonstrate that Bronze and Iron Age Sardinia was an active pyrotechnological and maritime hub, deeply woven into Central Mediterranean, Tyrrhenian, and North African trade routes. This paper introduces an innovative computational framework rooted in Knowledge Engineering and FAIR Linked Open Data (LOD) to formalize, query, and reproducibly audit this vast corpus of archaeological and textual evidence. We present the architectural design of the Rotta Aristeica semantic hypergraph, an open-source cultural heritage knowledge base featuring over 5,120 RDF/OWL ontological triples, 804 geodetic cartographic nodes, and 939 peer-evaluated discovery entities mapped against W3C, CIDOC-CRM, Schema.org, and DCAT-AP_IT standards. A cornerstone of this architecture is the Popperian Dual Hyperedge Pattern, which formally enforces epistemic demarcation by systematically separating consensus-driven academic data (VerifiedAcademicConsensus) from exploratory conjectures (SpeculativeHypothesis). Finally, the framework is validated through two real-world case studies: 1) the semantic federation of trans-Mediterranean Punic toponymy connecting Sardinia and North Africa (MQM ḤDŠ / Macomades in Planargia and Byzacena); 2) the systematic detection and correction of cartographic anomalies in collaborative open datasets (the rectifying of Panido to Pactya in the Thracian Chersonese isthmus). Keywords: Knowledge Engineering, Linked Open Data (LOD), Semantic Hypergraph, Nuragic Civilization, Mediterranean Protohistory, Punic Toponymy, Epistemic Demarcation, Digital Humanities, Open Science. 1. Introduzione ed Epistemologia: Il Superamento del Paradigma Isolazionista Nel corso del Novecento, gran parte della manualistica archeologica ha interpretato la civiltà nuragica attraverso il filtro dell'«isolazionismo insulare»: una visione storiografica secondo cui la Sardegna preistorica e protostorica avrebbe sviluppato la propria monumentale civiltà megalitica in una condizione di quasi totale impermeabilità rispetto ai flussi culturali del Mediterraneo orientale e continentale, subendo passivamente solo in seguito le colonizzazioni fenicie, cartaginesi e romane. Tuttavia, le evidenze emerse negli ultimi quarant'anni dall'archeometria moderna, dalla glottologia semitica comparata e dall'archeologia subacquea hanno definitivamente falsificato questo modello: La Pirotecnologia e la Circolazione dei Metalli: Le indagini archeometriche sugli isotopi del piombo (LIA) e sulle ceramiche nuragiche da esportazione condotte da studiosi di riferimento (Lo Schiavo, Campus, Sabatini, Begemann, Stos-Gale) hanno rivelato la presenza di lingotti di rame oxhide e bronzi nuragici a Creta (Kommos, Haghia Triada), in Sicilia (Cannatello, Lipari), a Cipro (Pyla-Kokkinokremos) e nella penisola iberica (Huelva); L'Integrazione Emporica Fenicio-Punica: Come documentato dagli studi pionieristici di Raimondo Zucca (1984), Sabatino Moscati (1986) e Ferruccio Barreca (1986), le comunità costiere occidentali sarde (Tharros, Cornus, Bosa, Magomadas) non costituivano enclavi isolate, ma erano snodi vitali della koinè marittima tirrenica e nordafricana; La Complessità del Corpus Documentario: La compresenza di fonti letterarie classiche (Erodoto, Diodoro Siculo, Pseudo-Scilace, Strabone, Solino, Tolomeo), registri epigrafici (dalla Stele di Nora CIS I, 144 alle epigrafi puniche e bilingui) e dati di scavo richiede strumenti concettuali capaci di superare la frammentazione disciplinare. Davanti a questa massa eterogenea di dati, la ricerca scientifica indipendente si trova spesso disarmata se priva di una metodologia strutturata. Il presente contributo illustra come l'Ingegneria della Conoscenza e il Web Semantico forniscano la chiave per organizzare, verificare ed esporre questi dati con trasparenza scientifica totale. 2. Metodologia: L'Ipergrafo Semantico FAIR della Rotta Aristeica Per superare i limiti dei database relazionali convenzionali (SQL), che faticano a rappresentare relazioni multi-dimensionali, incertezze cronologiche e discordanze tra fonti letterarie e contesti di scavo, è stata progettata un'architettura a Ipergrafo Semantico esposta secondo gli standard internazionali dei Linked Open Data (LOD) e i principi FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable). 2.1 Standard Ontologici e Modellazione RDF L'ontologia federata del progetto adotta e armonizza vocabolari semantici W3C standard: CIDOC-CRM (ISO 21127): per la modellazione di eventi storici (E5_Event), manufatti materiali (E22_Human-Made_Object) e attori/popolazioni (E39_Actor); Schema.org & Dublin Core: per le coordinate geodetiche (schema:GeoCoordinates), l'attribuzione bibliografica e gli identificatori digitali persistenti (DOI, ORCID); PROV-O (W3C Provenance Ontology): per tracciare la catena di derivazione e l'orizzonte critico di ciascuna fonte primaria. 2.2 Il Pattern della Biforcazione a Doppio Iperarco Concorrente Il contributo epistemologico più originale dell'architettura è l'implementazione del Doppio Iperarco Concorrente (Dual Hyperedge Architecture), concepito per applicare rigidamente il principio di demarcazione popperiana e prevenire qualsiasi deriva pseudoscientifica o sicofantica: Plaintext [ SCIENTIFIC ENTITY / DISCOVERY ] │ ┌──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ [ IPERARCO ACCADEMICO ] [ IPERARCO SPECULATIVO ] VerifiedAcademicConsensus SpeculativeHypothesis │ │ • Fonti primarie verificate; • Ipotesi esplorative di lavoro; • DOI accademici peer-reviewed; • Esperimenti mentali e analogie; • Dati empirici archeometrici (aDNA, LIA); • Demarcazione formale esplicita; • Glottologia storica comparata. • Testabilità popperiana futura. Iperarco del Consenso Accademico Ufficiale (AcademicConsensusHyperedge): Mappa esclusivamente evidenze archeologiche documentate, pubblicazioni peer-reviewed dotate di DOI e concordanze filologiche accertate; Iperarco dell'Ipotesi Speculativa (SpeculativeHypothesisHyperedge): Registra in modo trasparente e formalmente etichettato le ipotesi di lavoro, gli esperimenti mentali e le teorie esplorative formulate dal ricercatore indipendente, impedendo categoricamente che una congettura venga scambiata per un fatto accertato. 3. Nevertheless, state-of-the-art archaeometric analyses (lead isotope provenance, trans-Mediterranean dispersal of oxhide ingots, Nuragic metallurgy documented in Crete, Lipari, Cannatello, and Huelva), paleogenomics (aDNA), and semitic toponomastics demonstrate that Bronze and Iron Age Sardinia was an active pyrotechnological and maritime hub, deeply woven into Central Mediterranean, Tyrrhenian, and North African trade routes. This paper introduces an innovative computational framework rooted in Knowledge Engineering and FAIR Linked Open Data (LOD) to formalize, query, and reproducibly audit this vast corpus of archaeological and textual evidence. We present the architectural design of the Rotta Aristeica semantic hypergraph, an open-source cultural heritage knowledge base featuring over 5,120 RDF/OWL ontological triples, 804 geodetic cartographic nodes, and 939 peer-evaluated discovery entities mapped against W3C, CIDOC-CRM, Schema.org, and DCAT-AP_IT standards. A cornerstone of this architecture is the Popperian Dual Hyperedge Pattern, which formally enforces epistemic demarcation by systematically separating consensus-driven academic data (VerifiedAcademicConsensus) from exploratory conjectures (SpeculativeHypothesis). Finally, the framework is validated through two real-world case studies: 1) the semantic federation of trans-Mediterranean Punic toponymy connecting Sardinia and North Africa (MQM ḤDŠ / Macomades in Planargia and Byzacena); 2) the systematic detection and correction of cartographic anomalies in collaborative open datasets (the rectifying of Panido to Pactya in the Thracian Chersonese isthmus). Keywords: Knowledge Engineering, Linked Open Data (LOD), Semantic Hypergraph, Nuragic Civilization, Mediterranean Protohistory, Punic Toponymy, Epistemic Demarcation, Digital Humanities, Open Science. 1. Introduzione ed Epistemologia: Il Superamento del Paradigma Isolazionista Nel corso del Novecento, gran parte della manualistica archeologica ha interpretato la civiltà nuragica attraverso il filtro dell'«isolazionismo insulare»: una visione storiografica secondo cui la Sardegna preistorica e protostorica avrebbe sviluppato la propria monumentale civiltà megalitica in una condizione di quasi totale impermeabilità rispetto ai flussi culturali del Mediterraneo orientale e continentale, subendo passivamente solo in seguito le colonizzazioni fenicie, cartaginesi e romane. Tuttavia, le evidenze emerse negli ultimi quarant'anni dall'archeometria moderna, dalla glottologia semitica comparata e dall'archeologia subacquea hanno definitivamente falsificato questo modello: La Pirotecnologia e la Circolazione dei Metalli: Le indagini archeometriche sugli isotopi del piombo (LIA) e sulle ceramiche nuragiche da esportazione condotte da studiosi di riferimento (Lo Schiavo, Campus, Sabatini, Begemann, Stos-Gale) hanno rivelato la presenza di lingotti di rame oxhide e bronzi nuragici a Creta (Kommos, Haghia Triada), in Sicilia (Cannatello, Lipari), a Cipro (Pyla-Kokkinokremos) e nella penisola iberica (Huelva); L'Integrazione Emporica Fenicio-Punica: Come documentato dagli studi pionieristici di Raimondo Zucca (1984), Sabatino Moscati (1986) e Ferruccio Barreca (1986), le comunità costiere occidentali sarde (Tharros, Cornus, Bosa, Magomadas) non costituivano enclavi isolate, ma erano snodi vitali della koinè marittima tirrenica e nordafricana; La Complessità del Corpus Documentario: La compresenza di fonti letterarie classiche (Erodoto, Diodoro Siculo, Pseudo-Scilace, Strabone, Solino, Tolomeo), registri epigrafici (dalla Stele di Nora CIS I, 144 alle epigrafi puniche e bilingui) e dati di scavo richiede strumenti concettuali capaci di superare la frammentazione disciplinare. Davanti a questa massa eterogenea di dati, la ricerca scientifica indipendente si trova spesso disarmata se priva di una metodologia strutturata. Il presente contributo illustra come l'Ingegneria della Conoscenza e il Web Semantico forniscano la chiave per organizzare, verificare ed esporre questi dati con trasparenza scientifica totale. 2. Metodologia: L'Ipergrafo Semantico FAIR della Rotta Aristeica Per superare i limiti dei database relazionali convenzionali (SQL), che faticano a rappresentare relazioni multi-dimensionali, incertezze cronologiche e discordanze tra fonti letterarie e contesti di scavo, è stata progettata un'architettura a Ipergrafo Semantico esposta secondo gli standard internazionali dei Linked Open Data (LOD) e i principi FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable). 2.1 Standard Ontologici e Modellazione RDF L'ontologia federata del progetto adotta e armonizza vocabolari semantici W3C standard: CIDOC-CRM (ISO 21127): per la modellazione di eventi storici (E5_Event), manufatti materiali (E22_Human-Made_Object) e attori/popolazioni (E39_Actor); Schema.org & Dublin Core: per le coordinate geodetiche (schema:GeoCoordinates), l'attribuzione bibliografica e gli identificatori digitali persistenti (DOI, ORCID); PROV-O (W3C Provenance Ontology): per tracciare la catena di derivazione e l'orizzonte critico di ciascuna fonte primaria. 2.2 Il Pattern della Biforcazione a Doppio Iperarco Concorrente Il contributo epistemologico più originale dell'architettura è l'implementazione del Doppio Iperarco Concorrente (Dual Hyperedge Architecture), concepito per applicare rigidamente il principio di demarcazione popperiana e prevenire qualsiasi deriva pseudoscientifica o sicofantica: Plaintext [ SCIENTIFIC ENTITY / DISCOVERY ] │ ┌──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ [ IPERARCO ACCADEMICO ] [ IPERARCO SPECULATIVO ] VerifiedAcademicConsensus SpeculativeHypothesis │ │ • Fonti primarie verificate; • Ipotesi esplorative di lavoro; • DOI accademici peer-reviewed; • Esperimenti mentali e analogie; • Dati empirici archeometrici (aDNA, LIA); • Demarcazione formale esplicita; • Glottologia storica comparata. • Testabilità popperiana futura. Iperarco del Consenso Accademico Ufficiale (AcademicConsensusHyperedge): Mappa esclusivamente evidenze archeologiche documentate, pubblicazioni peer-reviewed dotate di DOI e concordanze filologiche accertate; Iperarco dell'Ipotesi Speculativa (SpeculativeHypothesisHyperedge): Registra in modo trasparente e formalmente etichettato le ipotesi di lavoro, gli esperimenti mentali e le teorie esplorative formulate dal ricercatore indipendente, impedendo categoricamente che una congettura venga scambiata per un fatto accertato. 3. title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning of Co-Adaptive Hip Exoskeleton Control (MARL-Exo) for Metabolic Energy Reduction
abstract: Objective: This study aims to determine whether a hip-exoskeleton policy trained in simulation, by co-adapting with a musculoskeletal human model under a metabolic-energy reward, reduces the metabolic cost of walking in new users without per-user tuning, and how mechanical-power shaping affects the learned assistance. Methods: We developed MARL-Exo, a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework in which a full-body human model (304 muscle actuators; randomized anatomy, gait, and speed) and a bilateral hip-exoskeleton policy are trained concurrently in two stages. The exoskeleton observes only delayed hip kinematics and its past commands; its reward includes muscle metabolic power from a physiologically based energetics model, alone (Metabolic) or with mechanical-power shaping (Metabolic + Power). The Metabolic policy was deployed and tested without retraining in eight healthy adults walking at 1.25 m/s, using indirect calorimetry. Results: In simulation, the Metabolic policy reduced modeled muscle metabolic power by 13.8% relative to no-device walking, versus 8.8% for Metabolic + Power. On hardware, MARL-Exo reduced net metabolic rate by 18.3 $\pm$ 6.6% relative to Passive in all eight participants. Relative to No-Exo, the mean reduction was 7.4 $\pm$ 10.0%; six participants more than offset the 13.1% device-wearing penalty, walking up to 24.2% below their No-Exo cost. Conclusion: A metabolically informed policy co-adapted in simulation transferred to users without per-user tuning and consistently reduced the metabolic cost of walking with the device, while explicit power shaping reduced the simulated benefit. Significance: Unlike per-user human-in-the-loop optimization, this approach yields a single population-level controller and allows assistance objectives to be screened in simulation before human testing.

title: How control allocation in AI-enabled travel planning shapes reuse intention: the roles of user experience, emotion regulation and psychological empowerment
abstract: Purpose This study examines how control allocation between users and artificial intelligence (AI) systems shapes reuse intention in AI-enabled travel planning and whether this effect operates through user experience (UX), cognitive reappraisal, expressive suppression, psychological empowerment and satisfaction. Design/methodology/approach Two scenario-based studies were conducted. A laboratory pilot (n = 92) validated system-dominant, shared-control and user-dominant planning conditions. A main online study (n = 463) tested the proposed serial process using confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modeling and 5,000-resample bootstrapping. Findings Control allocation significantly affected UX. More favorable UX increased cognitive reappraisal and reduced expressive suppression, and these two regulatory routes had opposite effects on psychological empowerment. Empowerment enhanced satisfaction, which subsequently predicted reuse intention. A supplementary analysis further indicated that AI usage experience conditioned the relationships between UX and emotion regulation. Practical implications AI travel planners should treat control allocation as an interaction-design decision. Modular editing, progressive explanations, reversible changes and adaptive control can preserve user agency while retaining the efficiency benefits of AI assistance. Originality/value This study extends continuance research by identifying the upstream psychological process through which satisfaction is formed under different control-allocation structures. It further distinguishes UX as an evaluative appraisal from emotion regulation as a subsequent coping process in AI-enabled travel planning.

title: FeatureArc: Benchmarking Coding Agents on Evolving Features
abstract: A software feature usually evolves over time: developers extend its first version as new use cases and requirements arrive, and each extension builds on code written earlier. Most feature benchmarks evaluate a single request on a fixed codebase. Feature evolution requires evaluating successive extensions on an agent's own earlier code and checking whether the feature remains correct. We introduce FeatureArc to evaluate coding agents on evolving features, together with a pipeline that constructs its tasks from repository histories. The benchmark combines dependencies between successive stages of the same feature, explicit requirements and interface contracts, and executable checks across four programming languages. The pipeline validates fail-to-pass (F2P) tests for new behavior and pass-to-pass (P2P) tests for existing behavior on the reference code before and after each stage. We evaluated 10 coding agents on 73 manually reviewed tasks of 2 to 10 stages. Each agent works in one persistent session and workspace without external test feedback or rollback. The evaluation reveals a gap between first-stage and whole-feature success: pooled success falls from 62.7% at the first stage to 28.5% when the whole feature is tested on the final code. Trajectory analysis identifies inherited defects as a common failure mechanism, present in 72.9% of failed later stages. These earlier errors often remain undetected: in stages following a failure, agents leave the earlier error unnoticed about 95% of the time, and their self-tests rarely revisit earlier stages. Evolving a feature autonomously, without human checks between stages, therefore remains a substantial challenge for current coding agents. At Tencent, the pipeline extends internal evaluations to this setting and guides the development of Hunyuan, Tencent's family of large language models.

title: CodeCap-Bench: Can Code Serve as a Good Video Caption?
abstract: Video captioning aims to preserve visual information through compact descriptions, predominantly using natural language. However, precisely expressing fine-grained spatial structures and temporal dynamics in natural language often leads to lengthy and potentially ambiguous descriptions. In this work, we explore Code as Video Caption, a paradigm where executable programs serve as a complementary representation of visual content through graphical primitives, layout rules, and functions of time. To examine whether code captions effectively preserve video information, we compare them with natural language captions on downstream question answering and video reconstruction tasks. Our results show that code captions achieve superior reasoning accuracy and reconstruction fidelity. Despite these advantages, realizing the potential of code captioning depends on whether current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can generate faithful code captions. To systematically assess this capability, we introduce CodeCap-Bench, which comprises 323 videos spanning five categories of structured 2D content, along with fine-grained annotations and a multi-level evaluation framework. Extensive experiments reveal that while leading proprietary MLLMs demonstrate promising code captioning capabilities, they still struggle to faithfully capture complex temporal dynamics, with open-source models lagging substantially behind.

title: OblivoneSort
abstract: OblivoneSort is a C++17 header-only, unstable distribution sort. It maps values to order-preserving uint64 keys, computes bucket indices directly, counts, prefix-sums, scatters, and recursively sorts buckets. An optional parallel header provides parallel root processing and depth-1 group sorting. It targets random and smooth numeric distributions, not TimSort-style structured data. Version 1.1.0 adds an opt-in bucket-index cache (options::cache_bucket_index). The cache is disabled by default, is used only when the effective bucket count is at most 65536, and adds about 2n bytes of memory. It is intended primarily for expensive custom keys and is not a universal speedup. Caching with B = n is not supported. 1.1.0 新增可选桶号缓存 options::cache_bucket_index,默认关闭;仅当有效桶数 不超过 65536 时生效,额外约 2n 字节内存。主要适合昂贵自定义 key,不是普适加速; 不支持 B = n 缓存。

title: Segmentation Confidence for Arbitrary CNNs
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNN) are widely used for medical image segmentation. However, they lack an inherent measure of confidence. Existing methods for estimating prediction uncertainty often require a custom network architecture and/or dedicated training setups and need to be trained from scratch. In addition, the deduction of a single confidence score per input from the uncertainty maps is not always straightforward. In this study, we explore voxel-based uncertainty estimation methods that can be added to existing segmentation pipelines without training from scratch. We also propose a novel method to estimate a single confidence score from the uncertainty maps. Our evaluations on different ROIs and modalities suggest that our confidence score can predict segmentation performance in unseen data.

title: Your Policy Is Secretly a Harness: The Decision Geometry of Agent Interfaces
abstract: Language model agents are post-trained and deployed through a harness, the prompts, tools, and control logic that present a task to the model and execute its outputs. Harnesses are often revised and judged by how an already trained model performs under them, which assumes that what the model learned under one harness carries over to the next. We ask what a policy learns from its harness and what survives when the harness changes. Under KL-regularized control, we show that the log odds of an optimal policy recover how strongly its harness favors each action over the others, so a trained policy carries the preferences of its harness. Deployed return then equals the ceiling of the harness, the best return it offers, minus the mismatch of the policy, the return lost to its own suboptimal decisions. Training changes only the mismatch, while changing the harness moves both terms. Comparing harnesses with a fixed model therefore mixes what each harness offers with how well that model uses it. In MiniWoB++, post-training makes a model's preferences specific to its training harness. Reversing the order of the observation fields leaves every optimal decision unchanged yet lowers a trained model's success from 85.0% to 19.2%. Conversely, every new harness that a fixed-model comparison rejects but that raises the ceiling outperforms the original agent after further training under it, and ceiling and mismatch measured beforehand predict these gains. For coding-agent harnesses on Terminal-Bench Lite, ceiling minus mismatch estimated with a stronger model as a stand-in for the optimum reproduces the accuracy ranking, while either term alone does not. Code is available at https://github.com/2020-qqtcg/HRP.

title: Student-AI collaboration in learning: A case of a student solving a Math+CT task
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is one of the emerging technologies that has gained significant interest in education. Its potential in supporting students' learning urges researchers to explore and investigate how it can be used effectively. In this study, we utilized ChatGPT, an AI-powered chatbot, embedded in the digital platform Fobizz to support students in solving mathematics and computational thinking (Math + CT) tasks. This study was part of a larger investigation into integrating CT into mathematics lessons. Through an educational design research approach, we developed Math + CT tasks that enable students to program spreadsheets to read numbers into text with the help of AI. One high school student participated in this pilot study. Data were collected from the student's prompts and communication with Chatbot-AI, as well as data from the cloud spreadsheet file. The data were analyzed through thematic analysis. Four themes emerged from the data, providing insight into how student-AI interaction has contributed to the use of AI in education.

title: When Visual Evidence Is Insufficient: How Instructions, Post-Training, and Internal Activations Shape Refusal in Multimodal Language Models
abstract: For reliable deployment, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) should recognize when an image provides insufficient evidence to answer a question and withhold unsupported answers. Yet refusal alone is not necessarily evidence of such recognition: models may refuse because of unrelated safety constraints or without identifying the missing evidence. We study how refusal on visually unanswerable questions is shaped by three sources of control: inference-time instructions, post-training, and internal activation interventions. Across three MLLMs on the MoHoBench benchmark, we systematically manipulate the meaning and placement of refusal instructions, compare supervised and preference-based post-training, and intervene on a refusal-related activation direction derived from naturally answered and refused examples. We find that refusal is highly sensitive to both the meaning and placement of instructions, with model-specific changes at the sample level that are obscured by aggregate refusal rates. Evidence-aware and general refusal instructions have stronger effects than an intentionally mismatched safety instruction. Post-training produces larger increases in refusal, but can also induce responses that combine refusal language with attempted answers. In contrast, activation intervention produces smaller yet transferable changes across prompt conditions, without evidence of indiscriminate refusal on tested visually answerable samples. These findings show that refusal is jointly shaped by external instructions, post-training, and internal representations, highlighting the need to disentangle evidence recognition from a model's learned propensity to refuse.

title: TAO: Tool-Aware Joint Scheduling for LLM-Based Agentic Serving
abstract: Agentic services alternate between model inference on clustered GPUs and external tools on distributed CPUs. In this scenario, existing systems (1) overlook tool-return readiness in service evaluation, wasting limited resources, and (2) use heuristic strategies to decide admission and placement on GPUs, resulting in suboptimal scheduling decisions. To bridge this gap, we present TAO, a tool-aware joint scheduling framework for LLM-based agentic serving. Its value interface combines near-term tool readiness, node-specific cache credit with time-aware decay, and token footprint; a dynamic program jointly selects and places waiting sessions under capacity constraints. Across the 12 reported model-workload-concurrency settings, TAO reduces latency by up to 26.8%, reduces mean time to first token (TTFT) by up to 36.3%, and increases decode throughput by up to 29.5% relative to the best evaluated state-of-the-art baseline for each metric.

evidence.title: TAO: Tool-Aware Joint Scheduling for LLM-Based Agentic Serving
evidence.abstract: Agentic services alternate between model inference on clustered GPUs and external tools on distributed CPUs. In this scenario, existing systems (1) overlook tool-return readiness in service evaluation, wasting limited resources, and (2) use heuristic strategies to decide admission and placement on GPUs, resulting in suboptimal scheduling decisions. title: Edit, Then Merge: Mitigating Interference in Batch Knowledge Editing
abstract: 대규모 언어 모델은 방대한 데이터를 학습함으로써 다양한 자연어처리 작업에서 뛰어난 성능을 보인다. 그러나 학습 과정에서 부정확하거나 편향된 정보가 포함될 수 있으며, 이는 모델 출력의 신뢰성과 정확성을 저하시킬 수 있다. 이를 해결하기 위해, 모델 내부 지식을 수정하는 지식 편집 연구가 활발히 이루어지고 있다. 그러나 다수의 지식을 동시에 편집할 경우, 지식 간 간섭으로 인해 성능 저하 문제가 발생한다. 본 연구에서는 이러한 다중 편집 환경에서의 성능 붕괴 문제를 완화하기 위해, 주어진 지식 집합을 MEMIT으로 일괄 편집한 후 편집된 모델을 원본 모델과 병합하는 새로운 프레임워크를 제안한다. 제안 방법은 원본 모델을 기준으로 편집된 결과를 통합함으로써 파라미터 간섭을 효과적으로 줄이고, 편집된 지식의 정확성을 유지함과 동시에 모델의 일관성을 보존한다. 실험 결과, 제안 방법은 MEMIT 편집기법 대비 다중 편집 환경에서 더 높은 정확도와 안정성을 보였다.

title: Bayes-Adaptive MDPs for Rollout Allocation to Enhance GRPO Training
abstract: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has demonstrated strong performance in LLM post-training. However, it allocates a uniform rollout budget to every training question, ignoring variations in question difficulty. As a result, highly difficult questions may receive too few rollouts to generate informative positive reward signals, limiting their contribution to training, while moderately difficult questions often receive more rollouts than necessary. In this work, we formulate the problem of difficulty-aware rollout budget allocation to maximize training utility under the same total rollout budget as standard GRPO. We propose AdaRoll-GRPO, which reformulates rollout allocation as a sequential decision-making problem and leverages a Bayes-adaptive Markov decision process (MDP) to learn an adaptive allocation policy. The learned policy is computed offline and applied during GRPO training without introducing additional online optimization overhead. Extensive experiments on multiple reasoning datasets and LLM architectures demonstrate that AdaRoll-GRPO consistently improves GRPO training performance under a fixed rollout budget, highlighting the effectiveness of adaptive rollout allocation for GRPO in LLM post-training.

title: AutoRSE: Evaluating LLM Agents as Recommendation Engineers for Self-Evolving Recommender Systems
abstract: Recommender Systems Engineer Agents (RSE-Agents), which use LLM-based agents to autonomously improve recommendation algorithms, are emerging as a promising paradigm. However, their capabilities and limitations remain poorly understood due to the lack of a unified, standardized evaluation framework and systematic trajectory-level analysis. To address this gap, we introduce AutoRSE, an evaluation framework spanning six representative industrial-grade recommendation tasks, and conduct a large-scale empirical study of three frontier LLMs across three widely used agent harnesses. Our results show that RSE-Agents consistently enhance the performance of backbones on five of the six tasks, with an average relative improvement of 16.1%, indicating that they can already autonomously improve recommendation performance. However, trajectory-level analysis also reveals that current RSE-Agents function primarily as engineering optimizers rather than algorithmic improvers: their gains are largely driven by hyperparameter tuning, training strategies, and model ensembling, while genuine algorithmic innovations are rare. Since the largest gains in recommender systems often stem from algorithmic advances, this behavior underscores a fundamental limitation of current RSE-Agents. To probe this limitation, we perform idea-injection experiments and show that agents equipped with innovative ideas from frontier research or human experts achieve substantially larger improvements than those relying on self-generated ideas. These results suggest that idea generation is a central bottleneck of current RSE-Agents, highlights a key direction for the future recommendation system research. Our implementation is publicly available on GitHub: https://github.com/Ray-Tiann/AutoRSE.

title: Beyond the Readout: A Latent Numerical Frame Shared Across Modality and Operation
abstract: When a multimodal model computes 17+35 from text or 91-39 from a rendered image, it produces the same answer, 52. Does it use one internal concept of number for both, or separate machinery for each path? Similarity metrics such as RSA or CKA cannot settle this question. They give the same score to identical and to rotated directions, and two representations can look alike only because both prepare the same output digits. We therefore use causal interventions. For four conditions (text or image, addition or subtraction), we learn a small subspace of Gemma4-12B-it's residual stream in which swapping coordinates swaps the model's answer. The subspaces answer three questions. First, do the conditions write numbers along the same directions? They do not. Reusing a subspace from text in an image on the same operation recovers only 53.2% of its causal effect. A single rotation and rescaling maps one subspace onto the other and raises recovery to 91.4%, so the conditions share one geometry expressed in different coordinates. Second, does this shared geometry only reflect the digit the model is about to print? To test this, we split each subspace into 9 directions that the output layer reads to choose the next digit and 13 directions that it cannot see. The 13 hidden directions still carry the number, yet changing them barely alters the digit being written. Third, what are these hidden directions for? A model must emit a multi-digit answer one digit at a time, so it can compute the full result early and keep it in reserve. When two numbers share their first digit, swapping the number in the hidden directions leaves the digit being written intact and redirects the next digit in 77.6% of cases. The model thus forms an abstract numerical concept upstream and unfolds it across time: multimodal representations share meaning through relational geometry across distinct coordinate frames.

title: Vision-Language-Action or World-Action? Just Action Models
abstract: The vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action model (WAM) communities debate whether control policies should inherit pretrained knowledge from vision-language models or from visual generators. The debate, however, bundles three separable choices: backbone initialization, the objective applied to future observations, and whether the machinery for that future loss is kept at inference. A gap between a VLA and a WAM therefore cannot simply be attributed to any one of them. We show that decoupling these choices yields a common framework for both families, which we term Just Action Model (JAM): a pretrained visual backbone with an action expert, trained with an action loss and a foresight loss. The foresight loss trains current-observation features to predict frozen encodings of the recorded future through a prediction head discarded after training, so no visual generation is involved in either training or inference, and the backbone can be chosen freely. We first compare objectives within fixed policy architectures, then evaluate the foresight recipe across backbone families. The resulting JAM policies outperform their matched FastWAM and ImageWAM counterparts on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus, and achieve similar or slightly higher success rates on RoboTwin. Compared with FastWAM, JAM improves the success rates from 97.0%/55.3%/91.2% to 98.2%/64.5%/91.4%, respectively. With cached foresight targets, JAM reduces estimated online training FLOPs per sample per update by 73% relative to FastWAM. Our results show that future supervision improves control without visual generation or additional inference machinery, and strong foresight performance is attainable with either generator-initialized or vision-language backbones. Project Page: https://y0uroy.github.io/JAM

title: Scaling Real-Valued Variables for Encrypted Inner Product Operations on Blockchain
abstract: 이더리움 가상 머신(Ethereum Virtual Machine: EVM) 환경에서 사용되는 솔리디티 언어는 정수 자료형만을 제공하므로, 실수 기반 암호 연산을 수행하려면 블록체인 외부에서 실수 데이터에 스케일링 인자를 곱하여 정수로 변환해야 한다. 이때 스케일링 인자가 클수록 정밀도 손실은 줄어들지만 연산 결과가 자료형의 표현 범위를 벗어날 수 있다. 본 논문에서는 실수 난수 행렬 기반의 Threshold Predicate Encryption (TPE)을 이더리움 스마트컨트랙트에 적용하는 사례를 통해, 입력값의 범위와 행렬의 차원으로부터 솔리디티 int256 자료형에서 오버플로우가 발생하지 않는 최대 스케일링 인자를 도출하는 방법을 제안한다. 추가로, 복호화 결과의 오차를 실측하여 유효성을 검증하고, EVM 상의 가스 소모량을 실측하여 성능을 분석한다.

title: Displacement Moments and Path-Terminal Separation in Brownian Interpolant Sampling
abstract: Brownian stochastic interpolants connect paired endpoint samples, yet their sampling error can depend on displacement moments even when neither endpoint has a first moment. For arbitrary Borel couplings, we prove early-stopped, target-to-output KL guarantees for standard Euler sampling from the true source. A fourth displacement moment gives an explicit $O(N^{-1})$ bound; a second moment suffices for fixed-law convergence as drift error vanishes. For one fixed coupling with no displacement moment above two, original bridge-path KL stays of order one, comparison-path KL is of order $1/\log N$, and terminal KL is at most $C/N^2$ on the same grid. The path decomposition identifies the information about the source discarded by Markov projection. When the original bridge is Markov, current-state Euler sampling instead has a second-moment $O((M_2+d)/N)$ bound; finite-entropy Schroedinger bridges for the probability Brownian reference are included. We also construct a current-state learner with expected output KL consistency from iid endpoint pairs. Numerical diagnostics illustrate the distinct errors. Conditional diffusion identities specify a restoration interface, while image controls find no iterative advantage over cheap probabilistic predictors. Uniform terminal rates for general second-moment couplings remain open.

title: MLE-World: Predicting Machine Learning Experiment Outcomes with a Learned World Model
abstract: AI research agents can propose, execute, and improve programs that solve machine learning tasks. However, executing each candidate program requires training and evaluating ML models, limiting how many candidates an agent can explore at each step. We introduce MLE-World, a world model finetuned from Qwen3.5-4B that predicts a program's terminal output (error traces, training logs, and validation scores) from its code and data description without executing it, together with a confidence score estimating the prediction's correctness. Because a prediction costs one inference call rather than a training run, MLE-World makes test time scaling (TTS) affordable for these agents. We build five TTS policies, guided by MLE-World, that compare several candidates per step by their predicted outputs: Sequential revision, Best-of-N, Pairwise judging, Fusion, and a UCB style rule that also adds an exploration bonus from this confidence score. Since predictions can be wrong, we run a candidate for real only when its confidence score is low. On 17 MLE-bench Lite tasks, MLE-World matches the real terminal output on 77.9% of held out programs, versus 41.1% for much larger prompted models. MLE-World guided TTS achieves up to 22.1% higher observed mean performance than the agent without a world model, with less real execution. Project webpage: https://mle-world.github.io/.

title: Static Type Analysis for Python via Declarative Inference
abstract: 동적 타입 언어는 널리 사용되고 있으나, 명시적인 타입 정보의 부재로 인해 코드 가독성이 저하되고 유지보수 비용이 증가하는 문제가 있다. 대표적인 동적 타입 언어인 Python은 타입 주석과 정적 타입 분석을 통해 프로그램의 안정성을 향상하고자 한다. 그러나 기존 정적 타입 분석기들은 낮은 분석 정밀도와 호출되지 않는 함수 내부에 대한 분석 불가능 등의 한계를 가진다. 본 논문에서는 이러한 문제를 해결하기 위해 타입 정보가 수렴하는 지점에서 교차 타입을 활용하여 공통된 연산만을 유지함으로써 분석 정밀도를 향상시키고, 선언적 추론 기반의 모듈화 분석을 통해 실행 여부와 관계없이 코드 전반을 분석할 수 있는 Python 정적 타입 분석 기법을 제안한다. 제안한 기법은 총 234개의 테스트 프로그램을 대상으로 한 실험에서 평균 F1-score 0.81을 달성하여 기존 정적 타입 분석기 4종보다 우수한 성능을 보였다. 또한 실제 Python 프로젝트인 PathPicker 대상으로 한 실험을 통해 큰 프로그램에 대해서도 합리적인 시간 내에 분석이 가능함을 확인하였다. 이러한 결과는 제안 기법이 높은 분석 정밀도와 분석 효율성을 동시에 확보하여 실제 Python 프로젝트에 효과적으로 적용될 수 있음을 보여준다.

title: WorkFactory: Turning Professional Intents into Executable Work for Scalable Agent Training
abstract: Scaling supervised training for working agents requires diverse professional tasks that yield reliable expert demonstrations. However, missing or inconsistent task information can obstruct teacher execution and weaken the resulting supervision. We propose WorkFactory, a scalable framework for constructing coherent and executable professional tasks. Starting from professional intents, information-level planning builds an information support graph to guide task instantiation, explicitly representing the dependencies and locations of information required for the intended outputs. Probe executions then identify support failures and guide repairs while preserving the intended work. We construct 112,686 tasks spanning 612 occupations and use the collected teacher trajectories to fine-tune Qwen models at 4B, 27B, and 35B-A3B scales, yielding the WorkPilot family. All three models improve over their respective base models across four professional-work benchmarks, with WorkPilot-35B-A3B improving from 879 to 1565 Elo on GDPval-AA v2.1. Scaling analyses reveal model-dependent diminishing returns, with execution length first increasing and then decreasing. Controlled component analyses show that planning and repair reduce probe-diagnosed task environment defects and improve downstream performance. The data and models are available at https://github.com/IQuestLab/WorkFactory.

title: Robótica Educacional e Aprendizagem Ativa em Matemática no Ensino Básico: análise de uma intervenção com semáforo e carrinho programável
abstract: Este estudo analisa como atividades de robótica educacional mobilizaram conceitos matemáticos e estratégias de resolução de problemas em duas turmas do 9º ano de uma escola pública de Antônio Almeida, Piauí. A investigação foi organizada como intervenção pedagógica de abordagem mista e caráter descritivo-exploratório, utilizando observações de aula, produções escritas dos estudantes, questionários pós-atividade, registros fotográficos e tarefas práticas com um semáforo programável e um carrinho robótico. As distribuições de frequência apresentadas nos instrumentos contabilizam 40 respostas em cada atividade avaliada. A tarefa do semáforo articulou sequenciamento, medição do tempo, raciocínio proporcional, operações aritméticas e lógica algorítmica; a atividade com o carrinho enfatizou velocidade média e conversão de unidades. Na avaliação referente ao semáforo, 65,0% dos estudantes alcançaram pelo menos 40% de acertos e 37,5% situaram-se nas faixas de 60% a 100%; na atividade do carrinho, esses percentuais foram, respectivamente, 62,5% e 40,0%. A análise de uma produção escrita representativa também evidenciou estratégias de conversão entre m/s e km/h e de aplicação da relação entre distância, tempo e velocidade. Os achados são interpretados como evidências contextualizadas de mobilização de conceitos e de participação dos estudantes, e não como prova causal de ganho de aprendizagem, pois não houve pré-teste equivalente nem grupo de comparação. Conclui-se que a robótica educacional pode adquirir relevância didática quando os artefatos tecnológicos são vinculados a questões matemáticas explícitas, à mediação docente e a oportunidades de testar, medir, calcular, comparar e revisar soluções.

title: CTBakeGS: training-free baking of photorealistic CT volume renderings into 3D Gaussian splats
abstract: Photorealistic volume rendering of computed tomography (CT) may convey anatomy intuitively, but it needs the CT data, dedicated software and a powerful graphics processor. Three-dimensional Gaussian splatting (3DGS) displays photorealistic scenes in real time on less powerful devices, but existing medical approaches train each scene for minutes to hours. We aimed to convert a CT volume rendering directly into a 3DGS model without training. Splats were placed on an adaptive octree of millimetre-sized cells. Their colour and opacity were computed on the graphics processor with the renderer's lighting, cell opacity was converted analytically into splat opacity, and faint splats were retained stochastically above the 1/255 opacity floor of standard 3DGS rasterisers. Six public CT scans (1.5-mm voxels) were converted with three transfer functions and compared with converged references by peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity and a learned perceptual metric. Two-million-splat models reached a PSNR of 32.6 +/- 0.9 dB for bone, 30.1 +/- 1.0 dB for contrast-enhanced vessels and 32.3 +/- 1.5 dB for skin and bone. A conversion pass (usually two or three per model) took 4-30 s on a current laptop and 9-60 s on a desktop with a 4-GB graphics card. On the laptop, the models rendered at 68 frames per second at 800 x 800 pixels. Training-free conversion produced real-time 3DGS models of photorealistic CT renderings in about a minute or less per conversion pass on ordinary computers, with fidelity that we consider sufficient for interactive viewing.

title: Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception
abstract: Multimodal perception forms the foundation of multimodal intelligence. In particular, spatial perception and multimodal long-context understanding are two pivotal tasks that underpin embodied AI and multimodal agents. However, synthesizing targeted, high-quality training data for these tasks remains difficult and costly. Our key insight is that these tasks share an underlying capability, which we call connecting evidence: identifying relevant visual facts, binding them to the correct entities, recovering their relations, and composing them into an answer. Crucially, targeted training data are far easier to synthesize for this capability than for these tasks themselves. To strengthen this capability, we propose EvidenceConnect, an easy-to-implement data synthesis framework that uses zoomed views of related regions within a single image to generate questions requiring comparison, aggregation, or chaining of visual evidence. To ensure quality, a reference answer is retained only when independent VLMs agree on it, and region-ablation tests discard questions whose answer survives the removal of selected regions. We then train base VLMs on the resulting data with RLVR, obtaining Zooming without Zooming v2 (ZwZ2). Although the synthesized data are not tailored to any downstream benchmark, ZwZ2 improves fine-grained and spatial perception, with further gains on embodied spatial reasoning, multimodal long-context understanding, multimodal agent tasks, and general visual reasoning. These results establish EvidenceConnect as an effective framework for supervising evidence connection and suggest that strengthening this shared capability leads to more generalizable multimodal perception.

title: Analysis code, models and verification data for "Explainability profiles of DenseNet201 and EfficientNet-B4 in retinal optical coherence tomography"
abstract: Analysis code, trained models, preserved outputs and verification materials supporting the manuscript Explainability profiles of DenseNet201 and EfficientNet-B4 in retinal optical coherence tomography. Contents and analysis populations. The package includes inference and analysis scripts, Keras and ONNX model files, image-identifier lists, expert-click annotations, attribution maps, per-image numerical outputs, summary-checking scripts and plotting helpers. Classification uses the original Kermany test partition (1,000 images); deletion/insertion uses its 750 pathology images. Expert-alignment analyses use a separately constructed 90-image cohort, including 74 original-test and 16 training-partition images. Current SHAP results. The current SHAP summaries and Figure S3 use the supplied original-run maps and per-image CSV. The attribution target is the labeled-class softmax probability for DenseNet201 and the labeled-class pre-softmax logit for EfficientNet-B4. The package includes image-level reaggregation of means, standard deviations, paired tests, effect sizes and overlap-retention confidence intervals. The earlier both-logit reconstruction is retained separately as an archived comparison, not as the primary manuscript output. Reproduction scope. Remeasurement of preserved maps and reaggregation of supplied outputs are distinct from regenerating historical attributions or repeating model inference. The README maps current Main Tables 1-2 and Supplementary Tables S1-S9 to the available files and documents reconstruction differences and missing historical evidence. This deposit does not claim that every historical manuscript value can be regenerated exactly. Consult README.md and the provenance and verification notes before running scripts; some analysis commands overwrite outputs in their working copy. Source images. OCT images are not redistributed. Obtain them from Mendeley Data, version 3 (doi:10.17632/rscbjbr9sj.3); the package identifies the images used in each analysis. Licensing. Code and verification scripts are licensed under MIT. Models, data and derived results are licensed under CC BY 4.0. Component-specific terms and attribution requirements are provided in the archive's LICENSE file.

title: Clearing the FoG: Training KG Agents to Retrieve the Evidence Behind Their Answers
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can answer many factual questions correctly, but a correct answer is not necessarily a supported one. For an LLM agent, a knowledge graph (KG) plays two roles: as a source of answers, it supplies facts that the model lacks; as a source of evidence, it supplies the supporting triples that make an answer traceable and auditable. However, existing KG agents treat the KG only as a source of answers: their training data carries answers but not evidence, and their training rewards check the answer but not the retrieved evidence, so agents often answer correctly without retrieving the supporting triples. We propose FoG, a framework that trains KG agents to retrieve the evidence behind their answers. FoG consists of evidence-grounded synthesis, a KG interaction agent, and an evidence-coverage process reward (ECPR): the synthesis recursively hides explicit entities behind verifiable sub-questions, so that every question carries its supporting triples by construction; the agent records the triples returned by the KG; and ECPR credits each supporting triple to the turn that first retrieves it. Experiments on three KGQA benchmarks demonstrate that FoG enables 3B--4B open-source agents to outperform substantially larger baselines in answer accuracy and evidence coverage, with zero-shot cross-KG transfer.

title: Dense Representation Learning and Differentiable Shape Modeling for Spine Landmark Detection
abstract: Spine landmark detection from spinal X-ray is a key step for estimating spine deformation severity, for building biomechanical models, and for pre-operative planning. We reframe anatomical landmark detection as a pixel-level contrastive representation learning problem, matching dense pixel embeddings with landmark prototypes. Surprisingly, even with a generic U-Net backbone, this formulation results in more discriminative heatmaps compared to the traditional heatmap regression paradigm, leading to improved discrimination between vertebral corners on distinct vertebra. Furthermore, we combine the resulting heatmaps with learnable shape priors over the global configuration of spinal landmarks to resolve ambiguities in landmark locations, yielding a simple and practical approach to spinal landmark detection. Our approach is competitive, in terms of landmark accuracy and clinical parameter estimation, with the state-of-the-art on the public AASCE dataset and on two private spinal X-ray datasets. Our code and pre-trained weights are available at https://github.com/BioMedTP/Pix2Point.

title: Enhancing T-HyperGNN via Node Feature Similarity-based Hyperedge Weighting
abstract: 하이퍼그래프 신경망(HyperGNN)은 고차원 집단 관계를 효과적으로 모델링한다. 기존 T-HyperGNN은 텐서 표현 기반으로 고차원 상호작용을 직접 모델링한다. 하지만 하이퍼엣지 가중치를 노드 수(cardinality)에만 의존하여 계산하므로 내부 노드 특징 유사도를 반영하지 못하는 한계가 있다. 본 논문은 이를 극복하기 위해 분산 기반(VA), 코사인 유사도 기반(Cosine), 두 방식을 학습 가능한 파라미터로 결합한 Hybrid의 세 가지 어텐션 방식을 제안한다. Coauthorship 및 Cocitation 벤치마크 5종으로 실험한 결과, 제안 방식은 5개 데이터셋 모두에서 T-HyperGNN 대비 유의한 개선을 보였다. 특히 Hybrid는 Coauthorship DBLP에서 +9.42%p로 향상 폭이 가장 컸고 Cocitation PubMed에서는 92.03%로 전체 모델 중 정확도가 가장 높았다. 반면 노드 특징이 희소한 데이터셋에서는 기존 모델 대비 낮은 성능을 보였다. 이를 통해 하이퍼엣지 내부 특징 유사도를 반영하는 어텐션 방식이 텐서 기반 접근이 유효한 조건에서 노드 분류 성능을 향상시킴을 확인하였다.

title: An end-to-end framework for uncertainty-aware validation of generative models
abstract: Density estimation with generative models is a common task in the physical sciences, for example in background estimation in particle physics. Existing machine learning techniques, however, lack methods to quantify uncertainties that can be propagated into a statistical test. That limits the validation of generative models to standard goodness-of-fit tests, in which the generative model is treated as exact (point-null hypothesis). But a model fitted to a finite training set is never exact, so if its uncertainties are neglected, any sufficiently powerful goodness-of-fit test will eventually reject it once the test set is large enough to resolve this estimation error. We propose SIGMA, an end-to-end framework combining density estimation with principled uncertainty quantification. We use Gaussian mixture models, for which uncertainties are tractable, and further construct a new goodness-of-fit test in which these uncertainties are profiled as nuisance parameters to account for the statistical error of the fit, promoting the conventional point-null test to a composite one. A rejection then signals genuine mismodeling rather than a test set large enough to resolve the error of the fit, provided the propagated uncertainties faithfully cover that error. We demonstrate the framework on a controlled two-dimensional toy model and on a collider physics benchmark modeling the QCD background process. With uncertainties included, the same model can be trusted on test sets up to an order of magnitude larger than the standard test allows. Our work thus provides a statistically grounded basis for a robust use of generative models in the physical sciences.

title: Algorithmic Monoculture in Machine Learning-based Site-Specific Fertilizer Recommendation
abstract: Machine learning recommendations are often evaluated one model at a time, despite deployment across interconnected decision makers. For continuous NPK fertilizer prescriptions, correlated errors can aggregate across farms and generate systemic costs. A model of shared and farm-specific recommendation errors links expected social loss to model adoption shares; the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index characterizes concentration effects when common model errors are independent and predictive risks are equal. A covariance-generalized formulation captures the dependence between model families. A two-model threshold characterizes when privately optimal monoculture is socially dominated, and a convex portfolio rule limits average private predictive regret. Nine model families across five Moroccan cereal systems provide a benchmark-based calibration. Under illustrative parameters and a 10% regret cap, accuracy-constrained diversification lowers modeled social loss in all five systems by 10.89-41.53% (mean 19.41%). Uniform allocation reduces modeled loss in this setting, but breaches the regret cap in every crop. Correlation sensitivity shows that highly dependent model errors attenuate the benefits of diversification. These counterfactual outcomes are not estimates of agronomic or monetary welfare; the framework identifies adoption architecture and error dependence as ecosystem-level evaluation variables.

title: Smart Home Anomaly Detection using K-Means Dynamic Threshold and Isolation Forest based on Multi-Sensor Data
abstract: 고령화 및 1인 가구의 급증으로 고독사와 사회적 고립 문제가 대두됨에 따라, 스마트홈 기반의 비대면 안전 모니터링 기술이 주목받고 있다. 그러나 기존의 이상 탐지 연구들은 수많은 센서를 부착해야 하는 고밀도 센서 환경을 가정하고 있어, 높은 구축 비용과 프라이버시 침해라는 한계를 지닌다. 이에 본 논문은 센서 밀도를 최소화한 환경에서 거주자의 장기적인 생활 패턴을 분석하여 이상을 탐지할 수 있는 프레임워크를 제안한다. 여섯 종의 비침습적 센서 데이터를 바탕으로 동적 임계값을 통해 설치 환경별 분석 기준을 다르게 적용하였다. 패턴 추출 로직을 통해 데이터를 외출, 수면, 실내 활동이라는 3가지 거시적 문맥으로 추상화한다. 이를 Isolation Forest 모델로, 이상을 식별한다. 실제 데이터로 검증한 결과, 제안 모델은, 외부 활동의 극단적 단절이나 과도한 수면 등 사회적 고립 위험군에서 나타날 수 있는 이상을 추출, 탐지하였다.

title: Game-Theoretic Solvers with Bayesian Opponent Modeling and Moral Rhetoric Framing for GLEE
abstract: We describe the agent we submitted to the GLEE Competition, which plays bargaining, negotiation, and persuasion games against a shared pool of human and AI opponents. The agent is built around three central components: a classical game-theoretic solver to compute numeric moves, an online Bayesian layer to estimate opponent archetypes, and a language model to write accompanying messages. We utilize Rubinstein bargaining for bargaining, Faratin concession for negotiation, and Kamenica--Gentzkow disclosure for persuasion, and adapt those models to live opponents using two separate layers: a Bayesian estimate of the opponent's hidden discount factor, reservation value, or signaling reliability, and a Thompson sampling bandit over five moral-foundation framings coupled with an evidence-intuition spectrum to establish message register. Most of the development effort went into the recurring problem that theoretically optimal policies perform poorly in certain live settings; we report associated failure modes, guardrails we built, and our hypotheses. We additionally evaluate our model over 13,200 Monte Carlo games against 11 synthetic opponent archetypes, an ablation of the opponent-modeling layer, and an extensive analysis of 9,337 live-game messages in which moral rhetoric framing in the persuasion setting is strongly correlated with whether the buyer purchased ($χ^2=616.7$, $p \approx 3.7\times10^{-132}$), surviving controls for quality, round, and configuration.

title: Do We Need an LLM to Know Why Sources Conflict? Decision Models for Knowledge-Conflict Typing in RAG
abstract: When the sources retrieved for a query disagree, the right response depends on why they disagree: a question with several valid answers, a contested topic, stale information and a false source each call for different behaviour. Cattan et al. (2025) showed that telling a generator the conflict type improves its responses by about 24 points, but that predicting the type is hard even for frontier LLMs. We study whether typed decision models, which return probabilities over fixed options in a single forward pass instead of generating text, can do this classification fast and cheaply. Using the CONFLICTS benchmark and the original paper's prompt verbatim, we evaluate all 11 decision models served by one commercial inference gateway, from 7 providers, against Gemini models on identical inputs. Asked directly, the decision models reach 50.0--67.0% accuracy; 10 of the 11 match or exceed Gemini 2.5 Flash, the paper's model (61.3%), at 4--39x lower billed cost (2 were free) and 2.6--6.0x lower latency. The current Gemini 3.8 Flash (70.0%) is significantly more accurate than 8 of them, but sending each decision model's least confident quarter of queries to it gives a cascade statistically tied with it for 8 of the 11, at 25--37% of its cost. End to end, answers generated with the types of 10 of the 11 follow the expected behaviour as often as with the LLM's types. Decomposing the taxonomy into yes/no questions lowers accuracy for every model, and a repair fitted on one model does not transfer. Pre-specified diagnostics show that dates play no measurable role and that sensitivity to source order varies widely between models. Decision models detect a planted false source less reliably than the LLM as hard labels, but their probabilities still separate planted from clean sources. We release code, prompts and all model outputs at https://github.com/Parv17k/decision-models-conflict-typing.

title: GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latents as a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents
abstract: Mobile GUI agents are typically fine-tuned 7B-scale vision-language models (VLMs) that generate each action as text. However, these VLMs decode every action token by token, and even agents that score candidate actions keep a large language model or VLM in the loop, making them slow and memory-hungry. To address these issues, we propose GUI-JEPA, to our knowledge the first decoder-free GUI agent policy built on a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA), which selects actions in the latent space of a JEPA encoder pretrained on unlabelled GUI screenshots. Its action- and region-conditioned latent predictor turns the screen latent into one latent per candidate action, letting lightweight heads score all candidates against the instruction in a single batched pass, without decoding a token. We further show that the scorer relies on this latent pathway and that the predictor is trained for the decision itself: a randomly initialised predictor does just as well as one pretrained on screen dynamics. On AndroidControl, GUI-JEPA is 2.8-4.0x faster on the same GPU than a Qwen2.5-VL-7B agent we fine-tune with the same inputs, while reaching 86-92% of its in-distribution accuracy with 6% of its parameters. Code is available at https://github.com/bcwang-sjtu/GUI-JEPA

title: JEPA-Inspired Latent Field Prediction for Sparse-Pilot MIMO-OFDM Channel Reconstruction
abstract: Accurate acquisition of full channel state information (CSI) is essential for multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) wireless systems, while dense pilot-based estimation incurs substantial overhead. Directly minimizing the prediction error over raw CSI coefficients is fragile in realistic propagation environments, since small-scale fading, mobility, local scattering, and small spatial perturbations can induce large phase-sensitive variations. Nevertheless, wireless channels contain strong spatial, temporal, and frequency-domain correlations that can be more predictably represented in a latent propagation-field domain. Motivated by this observation, we propose a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA)-inspired field world model, defined as a latent predictive model of the wireless propagation field, for sparse-pilot channel reconstruction. The model maps CSI observations into latent time-frequency tokens, predicts masked or future latent field states from historical multi-band context, and fuses the predicted latent prior with sparse noisy current pilots to reconstruct the full MIMO-OFDM channel. Ray-tracing experiments show that the proposed method improves normalized mean square error (NMSE) over pilot-only and direct reconstruction baselines, supporting latent field prediction as an effective prior for sparse-pilot channel acquisition.

title: Evolving Agent Teams
abstract: The rapid progress of software engineering agents drives interest in applying them to open-ended problems such as GPU kernel optimization. However, we find that existing coding agents converge to local optima on real-world, expert-written kernels (e.g., FlashInfer). We introduce Evolving Agent Teams, a multi-agent framework that escapes such local optima. It features (1) a central supervisor that diagnoses each local optimum and restructures a team of agents; and (2) a persistent file system that comprises a learning document, an evolution history, and per-team artifacts, grounding restructuring with accumulated experience. Under a matched token budget, Evolving Agent Teams consistently outperforms strong coding-agent baselines. With an extended token budget, Evolving Agent Teams generates a CUDA kernel that reaches 1.2x mean speedup over the production FlashInfer MLA paged decode kernel from scratch and wins on 36 of 47 production workloads from FlashInfer-Bench (0.86-0.99x on the remaining 11). It also demonstrates superior performance on tasks such as KDA prefill on AMD MI350X (3.01x over vLLM) and NVIDIA B200 (3.44x over FlashKDA), MoE expert-offload serving on Apple silicon (30.3 tokens/s decode for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next in MLX 4-bit on a 48 GB M4 Pro), and RoboDojo robot manipulation (62.1 on held-out seeds vs. 55.3 for the best leaderboard entry). Code is available at https://github.com/caoshiyi/EAT.
