title: Axiom Dynamics 3: Conservativeness and Invariance Rigidity—Dual Conditions for the Legitimacy of Axiom Transitions
abstract: Changes of the rule set of an axiom system—expansion, contraction, and revision—change the theorem set in the closure, but “what a change must preserve and whatit must gain” has previously lacked a machine-checkable compositional criterion.This paper establishes, on a finite Horn deductive system, an object-level three-waydecomposition ledger for transitions: any rule-set change induces a theorem set T toT′, and the difference is decomposed into the object-level gain set Gainobj = T′\T,the loss set Loss = T \ T′, and the invariant set Inv = T ∩ T′. The three-waydecomposition is complete and pairwise disjoint. Legitimacy is decided by a dualcondition: the protection core Core ⊆ Inv (Condition 1, losslessness), and Gainobjor meta-level gain Gainmeta is nonempty (Condition 2, gainfulness). Failure ofCondition 1 is an immediate veto and is not compensated by Condition 2 or bysyntactic-level gains; after Condition 1 holds, Condition 2 can fail independently.The criterion for meta-level gain is based on the carrier function Car(P,S): aproperty P constitutes meta-level gain if and only if P holds in the post-changesystem, its carrier is nonempty, and it belongs to Type A genuine acquisition (Phad a carrier before the change but did not hold) or Type B level addition (P hadno applicable carrier before the change and acquires a carrier after the change).Type B must be marked “level addition.” The termination of closure computationhas carriers and holds at both ends of the change and is not counted as meta-levelgain; savings in derivation depth and description length belong to the syntactic-levelledger and are also not counted.On the finite Horn fragment, universal conservativeness (closure equality for every fact set) is equivalent to redundancy (the conclusion of a rule is already derivablefrom its premises via existing rules). title: RynnWorld-Latent: A Cross-Embodiment World Model Conditioned on Universal Latent Actions
abstract: Learning controllable world dynamics from heterogeneous interaction videos is challenging because robot embodiments use incompatible action spaces, while human videos lack native control labels. We present RynnWorld-Latent, a cross-embodiment video world model that uses the 3D-grounded latent actions introduced by RynnLAM as a shared conditioning interface. This representation enables joint pretraining on human interaction videos, robot demonstrations, and simulation rollouts without requiring a common native action space. Built on a pretrained video transformer, RynnWorld-Latent combines global action tokens with an identity-initialized local pathway that aligns actions with future video latents. We pretrain on 23 datasets comprising approximately 553.5M frames and adapt the model to target robots through post-training. The framework supports two data-generation routes: digital teleoperation uses target robot commands to generate action-video demonstrations, while latent-action synthesis transfers source motion to an edited initial frame and pairs the resulting rollout with retargeted pseudo robot actions. Experiments show improved video prediction metrics on public benchmarks and two real-robot platforms, alongside qualitative action following when different action sequences share the same initial observation. Synthetic mid-training improves policy success rates on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus, and both generation routes improve real-world policy success rates over real-demonstration-only training in the evaluated settings. These results support universal latent actions as a scalable interface for learning controllable visual dynamics across heterogeneous embodiments.

title: Soft-JMI: An Identifiability Metric for Sensitive Data Based on Fuzzy Set Theory
abstract: 딥러닝 모델이 민감한 개인 데이터를 활용하는 영역으로 확산됨에 따라, 학습 데이터의 유출 위험을 정량화하는 프라이버시 평가 지표의 중요성이 커지고 있다. 그러나 기존의 거시적 지표는 모델이 고확신 상태에 도달하면 출력 분포가 포화되어 방어 모델 간의 미세한 차이를 구분하지 못한다. 본 논문에서는 이러한 한계를 극복하기 위해 자카드 유사도에 퍼지 집합 이론을 결합하여 개별 데이터 단위의 식별 가능성을 평가하는 Soft-JMI를 제안한다. 제안 지표가 멤버십 추론 공격자의 목적 함수와 수학적으로 부합함을 유도하고, CIFAR-10 데이터셋과 네 가지 지식 증류 방어 모델로 지표별 변별력을 평가하였다. 실험 결과, 코사인 유사도와 KL 다이버전스는 모든 모델에서 포화되어 구분이 불가능한 반면, Soft-JMI는 Standard KD(0.5877)에서 CKD(0.4682)에 이르는 뚜렷한 변별 폭으로 모델 간 차이를 정량화하였다. 또한 평가 데이터의 구성 변화에도 모델 간 순위가 일관되게 보존되어, 제안 지표가 고확신 환경에서 방어 모델의 식별 가능성을 안정적으로 평가함을 확인하였다.

title: How Many and How Much? Contrastive Learning with Negative Samples for Knowledge Graph Embedding
abstract: Knowledge graph embedding (KGE), a fundamental technique for knowledge-centric Web and KG-augmented AI applications, is commonly trained through contrastive learning with negative samples to learn discriminative representations. Despite its empirical success, two crucial questions regarding negative samples remain underexplored: (Q1) how many negative samples should be used for each positive sample and (Q2) how much should each negative sample contribute to learning? To answer these questions, we propose RADAR, a novel contrastive learning framework for KGE models with two effective strategies, respectively: (1) Risk-aware negative budget allocation quantifies false-negative sampling risk by modeling an open-world KG as a stochastic partial observation of its closed-world counterpart and adaptively assigns a negative budget to each positive sample based on its risk; (2) Distribution-calibrated negative weighting assigns negative weights by calibrating the weighting strength for each positive based on two complementary characteristics of the negative-score distribution: dispersion and concentration. Extensive experiments on 3 real-world KGs with 4 KGE models reveal that RADAR achieves the best KGE performance on average across all model--KG combinations and reduces sampled false negatives by over 90% compared with conventional fixed-budget methods.

title: Can LLMs Reliably Grade Olympiad Proofs? A Study of Mathematical Verification with LLMs
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have made remarkable progress on solving competition-level mathematics, yet their ability to verify natural-language mathematical proofs remains relatively underexplored. This gap is especially pronounced for Olympiad-level proofs, which require meticulous assessment of each claim in a long reasoning chain. Current proof verification thus primarily relies on expert inspection, which is costly to scale. In this paper, we present a systematic study of LLM-based verification in this setting. Specifically, we introduce a human-curated dataset of USAMO 2025 candidate solutions with expert grading, and conduct a broad evaluation of existing LLM verifiers across frontier models. We also propose TROJAN, an iterative self-critique pipeline for generating high-fidelity adversarial proofs at scale. Our comprehensive evaluation covers 20 models spanning seven metrics, two prompt styles, three inference methods, and three prompt templates, showing that state-of-the-art models still leave considerable room for improvement. To narrow this gap, we propose MABGrader, a Multi-Armed Bandit framework that reframes grading as arm selection over the discrete score space. MABGrader outperforms the SOTA ProofGrader by 26.4% in Quadratic Weighted Kappa and reduces grading error by 14%. Code and dataset are available at https://github.com/aziksh-ospanov/TROJAN.

title: Drift-Gated Ensemble Pessimism for Offline Meta-Reinforcement Learning Robust to Behavior-Policy Shift
abstract: 컨텍스트 기반 오프라인 메타 강화학습 (Context-based Offline Meta-RL, COMRL)은 정적 데이터만으로 새로운 태스크에 빠르게 적응하는 에이전트를 학습한다. 그러나 기존 방법들은 컨텍스트를 수집하는 행동 정책이 학습 분포와 다르면 정책이 학습된 적 없는 잠재에서 실행되어 성능이 붕괴하고, 이를 보완하는 고정 계수 비관주의는 환경별 튜닝과 과보수화 문제를 낳는다. 본 논문이 제안하는 DELPHI는 잠재 공간을 외삽한 뒤 디코더 앙상블의 합성 롤아웃으로 정책을 학습 분포 밖 잠재에서 미리 단련하되, 롤아웃을 따라 누적한 앙상블 불일치 (정보 드리프트)를 z-점수로 정규화하고 임계 초과분에만 비선형 게이트로 페널티를 부과하여 신뢰도가 낮은 합성 신호를 억제한다. 게이트는 정상 영역에서 페널티를 0으로 두어 분포 내 성능을 보존하고, 롤아웃 구조 파라미터는 환경별로 설정하되 정규화의 스케일 불변성 덕분에 게이트 상수에 한하여 전 환경 단일 값으로 공유되어 환경별 페널티 계수 탐색을 대체한다. MuJoCo 4개 환경의 행동 정책 분포 밖 (out-of-distribution, OOD) 평가에서 DELPHI는 최신 베이스라인을 일관되게 상회하였다.

title: Para-Gaussian Approximations of Random Deep Neural Networks
abstract: It is known that randomly initialized neural networks have Gaussian behaviour in the $n\to \infty$ limit. Unfortunately, this approximation can be poor for finite $n$ and gets worse as one goes deeper into the network. In this work, we develop a more accurate approximation that is \emph{slightly} non-Gaussian, which we call the para-Gaussian distribution and is constructed from the Hermite polynomials. We show how this para-Gaussian approximation can lead to a practical recursive method to approximate the deeper layers of the network. Finally, we apply this theory to linear neural networks (where things can be solved exactly) and to ReLU neural networks (where things can be approximated).

title: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
abstract: Interactive world generation requires models to follow successive commands while preserving relevant history and action consequences. We present Hy-Nomas, a video world model with an 8B diffusion backbone that supports free-form text instructions and continuous camera control across multiple interaction turns. It generates variable-length segments conditioned on current inputs and cached history. Our central design aligns structured video captions with action-aware causal attention: descriptive context remains accessible across segments, while action instructions are restricted to their intended temporal windows. A vision-language Prompt Enhancer (PE) translates user requests and multimodal interaction histories into structured conditions for the next segment. A multi-stage curriculum progressively introduces causal generation, text interaction, camera control, and training on model-generated histories, followed by diffusion distillation. In human evaluation, Hy-Nomas shows superior performance over existing world models. We release model weights, code and benchmarks, together with a lightweight adaptation workflow, to support reproducible research on interactive world generation.

evidence.title: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
evidence.abstract: Interactive world generation requires models to follow successive commands while preserving relevant history and action consequences. We present Hy-Nomas, a video world model with an 8B diffusion backbone that supports free-form text instructions and continuous camera control across multiple interaction turns. It generates variable-length segments conditioned on current inputs and cached history. Our central design aligns structured video captions with action-aware causal attention: descriptive context remains accessible across segments, while action instructions are restricted to their intended temporal windows. A vision-language Prompt Enhancer (PE) translates user requests and multimodal interaction histories into structured conditions for the next segment. A multi-stage curriculum progressively introduces causal generation, text interaction, camera control, and training on model-generated histories, followed by diffusion distillation. In human evaluation, Hy-Nomas shows superior performance over existing world models. We release model weights, code and benchmarks, together with a lightweight adaptation workflow, to support reproducible research on interactive world generation.

title: PENet: Pattern-Enhanced Feature Embedding Network for Few-Shot Cow Identification
abstract: 최근 축산 현장 등에서 비용 효율적인 비접촉식 개체 관리의 필요성이 대두됨에 따라, 소수의 데이터만으로 개체를 정확히 식별하는 Few-shot 기반 식별 기술이 중요해지고 있다. 이에 본 논문에서는 RGB 영상만으로 개체 고유의 무늬 특징을 효과적으로 학습하는 임베딩 네트워크인 PENet을 제안한다. 제안하는 PENet은 개체의 전체적 외형을 파악하는 RGB branch와 고유의 얼룩무늬 패턴을 집중적으로 추출하는 Pattern branch의 이중 구조로 설계되었다. 또한, 실제 축사 현장의 복잡한 환경을 사실적으로 반영한 새로운 Few-shot 개체 식별 데이터셋을 구축하였다. 다양한 Few-shot 환경에서의 비교 실험 결과, PENet은 기존 임베딩 네트워크 대비 우수한 Top-1 식별 정확도를 달성하였다. 결론적으로 본 연구는 복잡한 실제 환경에서도 소수의 참조 영상만으로 신뢰도 높은 자동화 개체 식별 시스템을 구축할 수 있는 효과적인 방법론을 제시한다.

title: SMEBENCH: Benchmarking Neural Music Editing with Synthetized MIDI Edits
abstract: Neural music editing requires a system to perform a requested change while preserving the musical content that should remain unchanged. Existing evaluations often lack a paired target edit, making these requirements difficult to measure separately. We introduce SMEBench, a large-scale benchmark of controlled music edits constructed by modifying symbolic MIDI performances and rendering matched source and target audio. Each example contains a source, an instruction, a paired target, edit metadata, and complementary descriptions. The benchmark covers twelve instrumentation, articulation, dynamics, and pitch operations and includes a balanced 3,600-example test set together with a smaller real-audio complement derived from multitrack recordings. The paired targets allow source preservation, target agreement, and textual compatibility to be evaluated independently. We use these references to diagnose common audio-editing metrics and benchmark six representative editing systems, showing that the metric used to rank a system can materially change the conclusion. The dataset is available at our repository.

title: A Dereferenceable Web Resource Structure with Rule Validation: A Case Study on Air Quality Observation Data
abstract: AI 에이전트가 역참조한 값이 허용 범위와 단위, 항목 간 규칙을 지키는지 확정적으로 검증하는 계층은 기존 데이터 명세에 없다. 본 논문은 자연어 컨텍스트, 의미·타입 명세(JSON-LD), 검증 규칙(SHACL·JSON 스키마)의 세 계층으로 구성된 역참조 웹 자원 구조를 제안한다. 대기질 관측 데이터에서 규칙 계층 유무와 표현 방식을 달리한 6가지 조건을 통제 실험으로 비교하였다. JSON 스키마로 규칙을 제공한 조건은 정상 값 오탐률을 0.67에서 0.03으로 낮춰 판정 정확성에서 기준선을 유의하게 앞섰고, 극한값의 경고 구분은 두 방식 모두 기준선을 앞섰다(0.95·0.90 대 0). 반면 SHACL로 제공한 조건은 판정 정확성을 높이지 못하고 사전에 정한 비용 범위를 넘었으며, 관계형 정합과 명세 모순 검출에서는 이점이 없었다. 검증 도구의 자발적 호출은 드물어 이득은 형식으로 제공된 규칙 자체의 효과로 해석되며, 두 방식의 우열은 실험 에이전트의 문법 친숙도에 조건부다.

title: Look Only When Needed: Certificate-Guided Visual Routing for Efficient Diffusion VLMs
abstract: Diffusion vision-language models (DVLMs) process their entire input at every denoising step. Since visual tokens make up 89-97% of this input on the benchmarks we study, most of the decoding computation is spent repeatedly processing the same image. Visual token pruning methods partially relieve this burden by removing part of the visual tokens, but they lose the removed information and still process the remaining image at every step. To measure how often the image is actually needed, we compare LLaDA-V's predictions with and without the image at every decoding step and find that removing the image changes a token being unmasked at only 22.8% of steps on average and at as few as 7.9%. We therefore propose LOWN, a decoding method that decides at every step whether to process the image and how many tokens to unmask. LOWN predicts the masked tokens without the image and processes the image only when this prediction disagrees with the last image-conditioned prediction. Agreement certifies the earlier prediction for reuse, and the number of certified tokens sets how many are unmasked in that step. We further observe that the need for the image differs across benchmarks, so LOWN's adaptive decision is needed rather than a fixed schedule. Without training or a tuned threshold, LOWN retains 99.6% of LLaDA-V's score on ten benchmarks at 35.3% of the decoding FLOPs on average. LOWN also generalizes across LLaDA-based DVLMs, composes orthogonally with visual token pruning, and runs under key-value caching for further efficiency gains. Code and project page are available at https://hyeon9698.github.io/LOWN/

title: Contextual Compression with Attention: Enhancing Input Efficiency for Long-Contexts in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: 검색증강생성(RAG)은 질의와 관련된 외부 지식을 언어 모델의 입력으로 사용하여 거대 언어 모델(LLM)의 환각 문제를 해결하고자 고안된 방법이다. 하지만 LLM은 추론 속도가 느리고 입력된 문서의 길이에 따라 모델의 연산량이 증가하므로 대규모 문서를 처리하는데 한계가 있다. 본 연구는 이러한 문제점을 극복하기 위해, LLM의 입력 효율성을 개선하는 ‘어텐션 기반 문맥 압축(Contextual Compression with Attention)’ 기법을 제안한다. CoCoA는 어텐션 스코어를 기반으로 문서 내 단어의 중요도를 평가하고, 가장 중요한 단어들만 사용하여 문맥을 압축한다. 또한, 단어 단위로 문맥을 압축하는 방식을 통해 어휘가 서로 다른 언어 모델을 압축 모델로 사용할 수 있고, BERT 모델과 같은 소형 언어 모델로 문맥을 압축함으로써 연산 속도와 연산량을 크게 절감할 수 있다. 본 연구는 연산 효율성을 개선하면서도 성능 저하를 최소화하였고, 문맥 압축 모델의 연산량을 단축함으로써 추론 속도를 크게 개선했다는 점에서 의의가 있다.

title: Same Verdict, Different Readers: Personalizing Fact-Checking Explanations from Relative Preferences
abstract: Fact-checking explanations help Web users understand why a claim receives its verdict, yet the same explanation may not satisfy readers with different backgrounds and preferences. We formulate Faithful Personalized Fact-Checking Explanation Rewriting, which adapts an existing explanation to individual readers while preserving factual fidelity. Rather than relying on reader-written reference explanations, we learn personalized rewriting from the relative preferences of LLM-simulated readers. However, this presents two challenges: distinguishing persona-specific preferences from general explanation quality and learning beyond a limited set of predefined explanation styles. To address these challenges, we propose Personalized Explanation Rewriting via Preference Learning (PERPL), a framework consisting of two components. Simulated Preference Construction derives persona-specific supervision from simulated reader preferences through cross-persona reciprocal pairing. Progressive Preference Learning first trains a lightweight rewriter on the constructed supervision and then refines it through exploration-guided preference optimization, enabling it to discover preferred explanations beyond the predefined styles. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PERPL outperforms much larger general-purpose LLMs in personalized preference alignment while maintaining high factual fidelity.

title: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Behaviorally Adequate Test Generation from Software Requirements
abstract: As large language model agents increasingly compile natural-language requirements into repository-level code, requirement-to-test generation grows in importance to provide validation constraints (or harness) to guide code generation. Yet it remains unclear whether current agents can generate tests that validate the required behavior when the implementation of that behavior is withheld. Existing test-generation benchmarks mostly focus on white-box testing, whereas the requirement--test-related study usually requires evaluation on semantic alignment between the given documents and the generated tests. We introduce Req2Test-Bench, a benchmark containing 5,086 execution-validated instances recovered from developer-authored behavior-driven development (BDD) artifacts in 8 open-source projects, spanning 5 programming languages and 4 BDD frameworks. Each instance pairs a natural-language requirement in Gherkin with its developer-written Test Implementation. Given the requirement, target interfaces of the required behavior, an agent must generate a complete, potentially multi-file Test Implementation. Evaluation of 8 agent--model--reasoning configurations reveals a substantial gap between execution success and behavioral adequacy, which is measured strictly as kill-completeness: a kill-complete test kills every mutant that the ground-truth test kills. The best-performing configuration, Codex with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, produces passing tests for 82.8% of instances, yet only 33.8% are behaviorally adequate. We find that (1) scaling up agents yields sharply diminishing returns in behavioral adequacy relative to generation cost; (2) under-specified requirements cause the information gap, including ambiguous setup and implicit expected outcomes; and (3) requirement-grounded harnesses that steer agent non-determinism offer a promising direction for improvement.

title: iOS and Android Interoperability for Secure Third Party AI Tools - Cross-Platform Execution Finality, Hardware Security, and Interoperability
abstract: Beyond AI Sandboxes and Permission Checks: A Technical Specification for Cross-Platform AI Execution Finality, Hardware Security, and Interoperability New here? Download the presentation first for a quick visual overview, then the full specification. The problem AI agents no longer just generate text. They run code, call APIs, operate browsers, move money, and control devices across iOS, Android, desktop, cloud, and hardware. An agent can be sandboxed, logged in, and approved by a permission check, and still lack the authority to cause the specific effect it is about to cause, at the moment that effect occurs. Sandboxes limit where an agent runs. Permission checks approve categories of action. Neither binds authority to the actual operation presented at the point where it takes effect. The core idea Computation is not authority to act. The specification treats computing an action and making it effective as separate, independently verified steps: Candidate Act → Non-Effective State → Protected Validation → Scoped Finality Authority → Finality Sink Verification → Controlled Effectuation A proposed operation stays non-effective until an independent Finality Sink reconstructs the actual operation and verifies protected evidence and scoped, non-bearer, single-use authority. If any check fails, the effect does not happen. What the specification covers AI-agent security: tool execution, prompt-injection containment, external-action authorization iOS, Android, and cross-platform interoperability for third-party AI tools Agent gateways, sandbox egress, credential release, and non-bypassable enforcement Trusted execution environments, kernel mediation, virtualization, and hardware command boundaries Multi-agent delegation, causal dependencies, conflicting operations, and revocation Cloud, enterprise, financial, robotics, and safety-relevant systems The full document contains the detailed embodiments, definitions, workflows, and algorithms. Run it yourself: reference implementation with 400 automated tests https://github.com/sangmdas/ios-android-ai-execution-finality A vendor-neutral Python and SQLite reference model of the core workflow. All 400 tests pass. It demonstrates: the exact SHA-256 commitment of a Candidate Act and its Non-Effective State; operation-bound authority checks: principal, tenant, route, resource, quota, expiry, and generation; independent Finality Sink verification of the actual operation; single-use scoped authority and replay prevention; revocation and ownership epochs; atomic consumption, plus crash and lost-acknowledgement recovery; causal receipts between dependent operations. bash git clone https://github.com/sangmdas/ios-android-ai-execution-finality cd ios-android-ai-execution-finality python -m pip install -e . python -m pytest -q # 400 passed The model is platform-neutral. It does not include privileged iOS or Android system hooks, TEE or hardware enforcement, or cross-system atomic transactions. Those mechanisms are described in the specification. See docs/LIMITATIONS.md in the repository. Independent review is welcome through GitHub Issues and Discussions. evidence.abstract: Beyond AI Sandboxes and Permission Checks: A Technical Specification for Cross-Platform AI Execution Finality, Hardware Security, and Interoperability New here? Download the presentation first for a quick visual overview, then the full specification. The problem AI agents no longer just generate text. They run code, call APIs, operate browsers, move money, and control devices across iOS, Android, desktop, cloud, and hardware. An agent can be sandboxed, logged in, and approved by a permission check, and still lack the authority to cause the specific effect it is about to cause, at the moment that effect occurs. Sandboxes limit where an agent runs. Permission checks approve categories of action. Neither binds authority to the actual operation presented at the point where it takes effect. The core idea Computation is not authority to act. If any check fails, the effect does not happen. title: Agent-Conditioned Routing: Diverse Reasoning Paths Within One Frozen Model
abstract: Generating several solutions can expose alternative methods, but additional trajectories often paraphrase one dominant approach. We investigate whether the conditional capacity of a frozen sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) model can provide such diversity from one problem prompt, without user-assigned roles, prescribed methods, fine-tuning, or model copies. Agent-Conditioned Routing (ACR) assigns $m$ parallel trajectories persistent, untrained shared/private expert-eligibility masks while preserving the learned, input-dependent token router. On a screened 126-question multi-mode mathematics and physics benchmark, with model judges reading the reported derivations in full, we count the number of problems yielding at least two distinct primary methods among soft-correct solutions in four trajectories. ACR reaches approximately twice as many such problems as the strongest temperature setting under GLM 5.3 (37.3 versus 18.7), and 1.67 times as many under GPT-5.6 Sol (45.00 versus 27.00), at matched output budgets. A blinded four-expert audit on a stratified sample of 30 problems also finds more multi-method solutions with ACR on both backbones, with lower correctness. Matched-eligibility ablations show modest multi-method count advantages for ACR, while token-resampled masks attain higher correctness. An informed sequential prompt elicits more diversity still, using previous solutions and explicit requests for alternative methods. ACR adds about 160 KiB of mask state. In a three-problem microbenchmark capped at 1,024 tokens, its latency and peak VRAM usage remain within 3% of batched temperature sampling.

title: CARD: Contact-Anchored Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation
abstract: Humans are dexterous, but traditional data collection paradigms such as teleoperation, kinesthetic teaching, and wearable exoskeletons force humans to act through the robot embodiment, bottlenecking their dexterity. Retargeting can avoid this. However, existing methods purely translate kinematics and ignore the real-world contact dynamics essential for task success. We present CARD: Contact-Anchored Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation, a simulator and object-free framework that retargets human demonstrations to robot actions by explicitly preserving contact force targets. CARD unifies human data sources including video, motion capture, and tactile gloves via a shared hand--contact representation and generates explicit contact force targets in addition to kinematics. To maintain these contact targets during hardware open-loop replay, CARD also introduces a tactile tracking controller. For video which does not contain an explicit tactile source, we present Vid-HACO, our video-to-contact model that sets a new state of the art. Across our video, glove, motion-capture data and the GRAB dataset, CARD maintains contact on 43--78% of contact frames, while kinematic and object-aware retargeting methods maintain contact on <10% and 22.5% of the frames respectively. Further, integrating our formulation into physics-based retargeting improves strict task success from 12\% to 32\% on GRAB dataset. Finally, we show that our tactile tracker is critical to reproduce demonstrated forces during hardware replay. These results establish that contact preservation via CARD is a scalable interface for transferring human dexterity to robots.

title: Developing Domain-Specific Word Embeddings from Unstructured User-Generated Texts in 3D Printing
abstract: 최근 3D 프린팅 기술의 확산으로 온라인 커뮤니티의 사용자 생성 비정형 데이터가 급증하고 있으나, 전문 용어와 구어적 표현이 혼재되어 체계적 분석에는 한계가 있다. 특히 범용 코퍼스를 기반으로 학습된 임베딩 모델은 3D 프린팅 도메인 특유의 기술적 맥락과 오류 서술의 의미 구조를 충분히 반영하지 못한다. 이에 본 연구는 3D 프린팅 온라인 커뮤니티의 대규모 비정형 텍스트로 Word2Vec Skip-gram 기반 도메인 특화 단어 임베딩 모델을 구축하고, 공정 및 오류 관련 핵심 어휘의 의미 관계를 벡터 공간에 투영하였으며, 성능 검증을 위해 실제 출력 오류인 ‘Stringing(거미줄 현상)’을 판별하는 분류 실험을 수행했다. 이를 위해 키워드 필터링 기반으로 구축한 60,346건의 검증 데이터셋과 모델별 ROC 분석 기반 최적 임계치를 적용하여, GloVe, FastText, SBERT 계열의 범용 모델 3종과 비교한 결과, 제안 모델은 동일 계열의 범용 단어 임베딩 대비 F1-score가 약 16%p 향상되는 경향을 보였으며, 재현율 0.74로 문장 임베딩 모델에 근접하거나 이를 상회하는 결과를 확인하였다. 본 연구는 향후 3D 프린팅 분야의 텍스트 기반 오류 진단 및 지식 구조화 연구를 위한 기초 언어 자원으로 활용될 수 있을 것으로 기대된다.

title: Euclidean Crowding-Driven Adaptive Euclidean-Hyperbolic Graph Learning
abstract: Hyperbolic graph representation learning has emerged as a powerful paradigm for modeling hierarchical data. Unlike Euclidean space, which exhibits polynomial volume growth, hyperbolic space grows exponentially with radius, naturally accommodating tree-like structures without the geometric distortion known as Euclidean crowding. Despite strong empirical performance, the theoretical mechanisms underlying hyperbolic embeddings remain poorly understood. In this work, we provide a geometric quantifcation research for Euclidean crowding, a generalization-theoretic explanation for the superiority of hyperbolic space on hierarchical data, and further develop an adaptive Euclidean-hyperbolic fusion learning framework toward bridging this gap. Specifically, we \textbf{first} establish a geometric quantification of Euclidean crowding by analyzing layer-wise minimum separation in node embeddings, proving that fixed-dimensional Euclidean embeddings of tree-like graphs inevitably exhibit layer-wise crowding that leads to weaker margin-based generalization bounds. \textbf{Second}, we provide a generalization-bound for the superiority of hyperbolic geometry on hierarchical data. \textbf{Third}, we propose EH-Fusion, a geometry-adaptive framework that lifts Euclidean GNN representations into hyperbolic space via exponential mapping and adaptively fuses both geometries based on node-level neighborhood expansion patterns. Extensive experiments validate our theoretical insights and demonstrate the effectiveness of EH-Fusion on benchmark datasets.

title: When to Intervene? An Empirical Study of Errors and Self-Recovery in LLM Agents
abstract: LLM agents interact with Web services to perform tasks on users' behalf. Errors during these interactions can disrupt execution and prevent task completion, motivating external intervention. However, agents may self-recover through continued execution, raising the question of when to intervene and when to wait for self-recovery. We present an empirical study of errors and self-recovery in LLM agents. We construct ReInBench, a dataset containing 1,259 agent traces and 1,403 error events across computer-use and Web tasks. Our study examines how often and how quickly agents self-recover, how self-recovery relates to subsequent execution and task completion, and whether self-recovery can be predicted when an error occurs. We find that 725 error events self-recover, often within a few steps, with self-recovery performance differing across Execution LLMs. Self-recovery can also help agents recover from subsequent errors of the same type and support overall task completion. Intervention should therefore prioritize errors unlikely to self-recover, while allowing agents to continue when self-recovery is likely. Building on these empirical findings, we propose ReCoF, a method that predicts whether an error will self-recover to inform whether additional intervention is needed. ReCoF achieves an average relative improvement of 9.02% in Macro-F1 over the strongest baseline on ReInBench. Our code and data can be found at https://method-notes.github.io/ReCoF/.

title: NativeTrust: library, study scripts and results for "Re-proving native_decide facts in Lean's kernel: a study of 16 public packages and a converter"
abstract: The NativeTrust library for Lean 4, with its package add-ons, the drivers, aggregators and per-fact results of the study, the kernel supplements, the runs on the author's own published results and the tests, for the paper "Re-proving native_decide facts in Lean's kernel: a study of 16 public packages and a converter" (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23628414). The library is also available as a Lake package from github.com/tejasvi/native-trust (tag v1.0.0, commit aabef35). The code is licensed under Apache 2.0, except one package add-on that contains code from minidregg and is licensed under AGPL-3.0-or-later; the results and data are licensed under CC BY 4.0. Abstract of the paper. Lean's native_decide proves a decidable proposition by running compiled code and adds an axiom that records the result. Mathlib refuses such axioms, and so do the gates of Lean 4.35 (lake check and Comparator) and the independent proof checkers. We present NativeTrust, a Lean library that re-proves the recorded facts by kernel evaluation without editing the projects that contain them, and names the blocking constant when it finds one. Across the 52,821 native facts in 16 public packages (counting only built modules whose source names a native tactic), nine packages converted at least 90% of their facts, and the other seven converted at most 39%. The pooled rate is 98.0%, but one package contributes 87% of the facts, and the rate without the three largest packages is 65.9%. With all of the converter's transformations switched off, plain kernel evaluation alone reproduced 51,307 of 51,329 re-run conversions, so nearly every fact that converted never needed compiled evaluation. Of the other 22, six need their checks split into smaller declarations, five of them only because a static check caps the unsplit evaluation. The remaining 16 evaluate a definition compiled through WellFounded.fix. For these we give a fuel-indexed replacement, proved from the unfolding equation, that reduces no accessibility proofs, and it converts the two functions we tested on a nightly that contains core PR #14892. A one-import switch, which tries decide +kernel first, removed all 1,113 native axioms from lido-srv3 and from cvc5/logos's ten largest modules, with build time changed by at most 2%. It removed 36% of the native axioms of a random sample of 24 packages at 1.3 times the build time, and 21 of the 24 still built. A source rewriter replaces native_decide by decide +kernel wherever the kernel proves the facts within a per-fact budget. It removed 30% of the sample's native axioms (25% in the median package) and kept every build within 1.7 times its original build time. Without the budget it removed 54% (76% in the median package) but made one build 143.5 times slower. In both settings 23 of the 24 packages still built. Of the study's 1,057 failures, 825 are traced to a construct that the kernel cannot evaluate, 585 of them to iterator-based string functions. All but two of the 232 untraced failures exceed our time, memory or recursion-depth limits, mostly in the converter's own search for split points. Extensions made after the study address these causes: linear evaluation of string literals and proved replacements for string functions; cast-free decidability instances; rewriting of definitions that occur in types; budgets, structured checks and sharding for large checks; and a kernel-checked route for bv_decide with a bit-blaster written for the kernel. That route converts all 213 bv_decide facts of the study and the sample. BerryEsseen, the source of 569 of the 585 string-function failures, now converts all 579 of its facts. Some of the extensions were developed against the random sample's failures, and they raised its pooled rate from 44.9% to 68.8% and its per-package median from 77.8% to 100%. We produced kernel supplements for three packages, 1,594 theorems in all: one for every theorem whose native facts all converted, in the modules counted above. Each states the same proposition as its original, or a definitionally equal one, and uses only the standard axioms. All of them passed nanoda, while con-ron accepted 246 of the 248 supplement modules. The hand-built kernel versions of our own published results took about 1.03 million CPU-hours to build. The converter replaced two of them at about their cost and gave kernel proofs of 543 of the 770 core theorems of a result that had none, but no headline theorem converted in the 16 other results that we ran, where most facts exceeded our time, memory or recursion-depth limits.

It removed 30% of the sample's native axioms (25% in the median package) and kept every build within 1.7 times its original build time. Without the budget it removed 54% (76% in the median package) but made one build 143.5 times slower. In both settings 23 of the 24 packages still built. We produced kernel supplements for three packages, 1,594 theorems in all: one for every theorem whose native facts all converted, in the modules counted above. All of them passed nanoda, while con-ron accepted 246 of the 248 supplement modules. The hand-built kernel versions of our own published results took about 1.03 million CPU-hours to build. title: The Geometry of Manifold Learning: Singular foliations via Deep Learning models
abstract: Deep learning algorithms have become widely used and successful across a wide range of tasks. A key challenge is determining whether these algorithms truly capture the intrinsic geometry of their training data in order to better understand what they learn from data. In this theoretical work, we explore a new geometric structure defined on the data space by a trained neural network through the Data Information Matrix (DIM), a variation of the Fisher Information Matrix. This new geometric structure is a foliation and the main focus of this work is to explore the non-smooth case of ReLU activation functions, where traditional geometric tools often fail. The foliation is defined through a distribution spanned by the columns of the DIM. We first prove that this distribution is non-smooth in the sense of distributions, rendering the existence of an associated foliation much more complex. To circumvent this issue, we introduce a smoothed version of this distribution that differs from the original only on a set of measure zero. Finally, we prove that this smoothed distribution induces a singular foliation on the data space, which is based on the data the network has been trained with. Our theoretical contributions provide a geometric framework to better understand how neural networks organize their input space in non-smooth settings, bridging differential geometry and deep learning theory.

title: Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-Uni: Elastic Self-Refining Unified Diffusion LLM with Cross-Paradigm On-Policy Distillation
abstract: We propose Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-Uni (NLD-Uni), a unified discrete diffusion large language model (DLLM) for visual understanding and generation tasks. Compared with prior unified diffusion models, NLD-Uni introduces two major innovations. First, we propose a unified cross-paradigm on-policy distillation (OPD) framework that successfully transfers the visual understanding ability of autoregressive VLMs and visual generation ability of continuous flow models, to a unified DLLM. Second, NLD-Uni incorporates a novel progressive self-refining diffusion process that gradually corrupts each token across multiple steps during training, as opposed to adopting the conventional masked diffusion formulation that directly corrupts a clean image token to an uninformative mask token. At inference, this design allows NLD-Uni to make intermediate commit to a token, enabling progressive self-refinement for better visual quality. Through extensive experiments, we show that NLD-Uni achieves state-of-the-art performance among unified DLLMs on diverse tasks including visual question-answering, multi-modal reasoning, object grounding, text-to-image generation, and image editing.

title: Uncovering Why LLMs Fail: From Internal Mechanisms to Adversarial Reasoning Trajectories
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are usually evaluated by final-output correctness or safety, yet an endpoint label does not reveal how a failure develops throughout the reasoning process. We therefore ask whether ordinary reasoning failures and adversarially induced failures can be characterized using the same internal coordinates. Towards this end, we in this paper study a white-box diagnostic framework CauTrace to disclose the root-cause of why LLM fails from three fundamental inspections: Functional States, Propagation of Representation, Temporal-State Coordination and Reasoning Trajectory. First, seven functional states are creatively defined to represent the support and constraint processing in LLMs. Second, the propagation of representation change measures how the changes among the seven states persist across subsequent Transformer blocks. Third, temporal-state coordination and trajectory topology characterize when the commitment and verification occur relative to the support, and how the dominant state sequence evolves over the full inference process. Finally, we evaluate CauTrace on both clean reasoning failures and paired adversarial perturbations. Across Qwen and LLaMA-family models, the failed traces show weaker Attention-MLP agreement on support-state updates and less verification activity relative to commitment, while the exact representation-level signatures and timing shifts vary by architecture. Held-out repair and steering tests demonstrate consistent operational signals that were in line with our claims for certain models and specific settings, with aligned steering producing the predicted directional changes in process measures. Overall, CauTrace provides a unified diagnostic framework for analyzing failure dynamics through changes in support, commitment, and verification, which would shed light on the in-depth research on LLM security.

title: LociArt: A Unified Paradigm for Free-Style Local Video Stylization
abstract: Video stylization typically transforms entire scenes, while local artistic editing requires precise region--style association, spatial control, and temporal consistency. We introduce LociArt, a unified paradigm for free-style local video stylization that explicitly specifies where to stylize and what style to apply while preserving non-target content. At its core, GRNStyle builds on Generative Refinement Networks (GRN) and introduces a polar style-aware mask that embeds style identities as equal-norm directions within selected regions. Complementary representation--geometry conditioning combines encoded mask features with raw-mask spatial support, integrating spatiotemporal context with geometric control. To provide paired supervision, we develop an automated pipeline combining global stylization, video object removal, matting, and compositing, and construct the LociArt-100K Dataset with 100K local stylization pairs. We further establish the LociArt Benchmark, comprising 80 source videos and 84 target masks covering 168 foreground/background stylization cases, with a Style Prototype Similarity (SPS) evaluation scheme for regional style quality and complementary measures of non-target preservation and temporal consistency. Experiments show that GRNStyle outperforms existing methods in regional style quality and spatial control while maintaining strong temporal consistency. Qualitative examples further illustrate joint stylization of multiple regions with the same or different learned styles, despite training only on single-region, single-style pairs. Together, these components provide a unified foundation for learning and evaluating controllable local video stylization. Project page: https://higherhu.github.io/lociart/.

title: RF Fingerprint-Based Identification of IoT Devices Using Meta-ELM Classifiers
abstract: The increasing popularity of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has made them vulnerable to attackers, making customized security measures difficult due to limited resources. To address this issue, RF fingerprints, features of the physical layer of wireless signals, are being used to identify and authenticate IoT devices. This study uses low-cost software-defined radio (SDR), a single-board computer, and open-source software to capture and record RF signals. The captured signals are analyzed using the Hilbert transform to determine features for classification. Various statistical methods are applied to select the most relevant features, with the Minimum Redundancy and Maximum Relevance technique further reducing feature size. For the first time in RF fingerprinting, ELM-based Meta-ELM, Meta Multilayer ELM (Meta-MLELM), and Meta Constrained Mixed ELM (Meta-CMELM) algorithms are used as classifiers for device identification. The performance of these classifiers is evaluated based on the RF fingerprint dataset, which consist of 3752 raw signals from 7 devices. The Meta-MLELM classifier has an accuracy rate of 88%, while the Meta-ELM classifier has an accuracy rate of around 90%. The Meta-CMELM classifier performs with an accuracy rate of 92%.

title: TRIDENT-Seq: Profile-Matched Prefix-Future Contrast for Label-Efficient Payment Risk Modeling
abstract: Ant International accumulates large volumes of transaction history across users and payment businesses. Confirmed fraud and chargeback outcomes, by contrast, are scarce, delayed, and specific to each business. A single encoder pretrained on unlabeled histories could serve all businesses, but only if pretraining captures the behavior that separates risk. Coarse activity differences can make contrastive pretraining on transaction logs too easy: transaction volume, amount, and timing can distinguish a history's continuation from arbitrary candidates without modeling how payment resources are used. We present TRIDENT-Seq, a transaction foundation model trained with Prefix-Future Contrast (PFC). PFC matches each prefix to a summary of its subsequent behavior among candidates with similar activity profiles; activity prediction and dispersion regularization act on the encoder output. Across three production payment businesses, the pretrained encoder improves average precision (AP) and recall at a 0.5% intervention budget over architecture-matched scratch training in all six business-budget settings. With a fixed validation set, it exceeds full-label scratch training in mean AP and recall using 10% of the training labels on Wallet and 25% on Shopping and SME. Pretraining only on another business's histories still helps. Replacing profile-matched candidates with random ones cuts recall from 24.62% to 5.64%. In Ant International's deployment evaluation, recorded amount-based chargeback and overall loss rates are 37.7% and 37.9% lower than those of the previous XGBoost-based system under the same intervention budget.

title: High-Fidelity Aerostructural Dataset of Transonic Wings in Cruise Conditions
abstract: Recent advances in machine learning (ML) have the potential to substantially accelerate aircraft wing design, a process that has traditionally required extensive high-fidelity simulation and design iteration. Existing public datasets for ML-based wing design have focused primarily on aerodynamic performance, with limited consideration of the multidisciplinary interactions that govern practical aircraft design. In particular, efficient wing design requires simultaneous consideration of aerodynamic performance and structural integrity, yet no publicly available datasets capture this coupled aerostructural behavior at high-fidelity. To address this need, a high-fidelity multidisciplinary dataset for static aerostructural analysis of transonic wings is introduced. The dataset includes 2471 samples, along with three out-of-distribution samples. The wing planform geometry is parameterized by span, sweep, dihedral, tip chord, and tip twist, while the airfoil cross-sections are parameterized using the class-shape transformation method. The analysis is further parameterized by Mach number, angle of attack, altitude, and structural load factor. The utility of the dataset is demonstrated by training state-of-the-art ML models to predict aerodynamic surface quantities, integrated aerodynamic performance quantities, and the failure distribution of the wingbox. ML models achieve at most 0.0309 normalized root mean squared error (NRMSE) in the prediction of aerodynamic quantities and at most 0.1189 NRMSE in the prediction of failure distribution of the wingbox. By providing coupled aerodynamic and structural responses for a diverse set of transonic wings, this dataset establishes a benchmark for developing, evaluating, and comparing multi-physics ML models for wing design. Broadly, it is intended to encourage creation of similar high-fidelity multi-physics benchmark datasets across engineering domains.

title: Dialetheism and Dimathematism
abstract: In ‘One Heresy and One Orthodoxy: on Dialetheism, Dimathematism, and the Normativity of Logic’, Wansing (2022/2024) defines a notion he calls dimathematism , which, he says, is an alternative to dialetheism. Dimathematism is a perfectly coherent view, but it is not, I think, an alternative to dialetheism. In this chapter I will explain why.

title: SO-101 Bench: Accessible Spatial Manipulation
abstract: Low-cost arms such as the SO-101 have become the most common entry point to robot learning, yet no released policy performs spatially constrained, language-conditioned tasks on them out of the box, and existing SO-101 benchmarks run only on physical hardware with simple tasks and few held-out objects. We introduce SO-101 Bench, a simulated benchmark for language-conditioned spatial manipulation built on an Isaac Lab digital twin of a real SO-101 setup. It has four tasks scored as five families, 138 objects in seen, unseen-instance and unseen-class splits, 916 evaluation episodes with subsets for held-out appearances, rotate-to-fit planning and occlusion memory, and 3,629 simulated demonstrations on which every learned policy is fine-tuned under an equal compute budget. The twin ranks policies as the real robot does: five policies trained without real data, four VLAs and an LLM agent, keep their exact ranking when the same weights run on the physical arm in an unseen environment with unseen objects (Spearman rho = 1.00, MMRV = 0.000), although simulation overestimates success. Across nine VLAs and world-action models, the best learned policies score near 61%, with spatial placement, unseen object classes and rotate-to-fit planning remaining open. An LLM agent that writes code and hands grasping to a learned policy scores 83.2%, and an ablation shows that this lead comes from the choice of harness and the choice of language model.

title: S3CNN: Spin-weighted Smoothing Spherical CNN for Learning from Scalar and Vector Fields on Spheres
abstract: Analyzing scalar and vector fields on the sphere, such as temperature or wind speed and direction on Earth, is a difficult task. Models should respect both the rotational symmetries of the sphere and the inherent symmetries of the vector fields. A class of equivariant models has emerged, which process these spherical signals by applying group convolutions in Fourier space with respect to the three-dimensional rotation group and have taken the name of spherical CNNs. In their original formulation, however, spherical CNNs are computationally expensive, and thus intractable for most real-world applications. Spin-weighted spherical CNNs were proposed as a way of reducing the scaling in the number of filter-coefficients with increased bandwidth, but the resulting architectures impose constraints on the choice of convolution kernels and activation functions in order to preserve the desired signal properties. In this paper, we introduce a deep learning architecture that occupies the middle ground: less demanding than the original spherical CNNs, yet employing a richer class of convolution kernels and activation functions, and suitable for signals consisting of both scalar and vector fields on the sphere. Experiments show that this architecture generally outperforms standard CNNs and often matches or exceeds the performance of spin-weighted spherical CNNs trained under comparable conditions. The advantage over spin-weighted spherical CNNs is not uniform across all tasks, however, and we present ablation studies in which we observe that incorporating the interaction between different spins in the hidden layers narrows this gap.

title: Lookahead Generative AI: A Unified Framework for Predictive Action Selection, Future-Outcome Modeling, and Modular Research Development
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence systems increasingly operate as interactive, multi-step processes rather than isolated input-to-output functions. Large language models generate and revise text, coding systems construct software, multimodal models coordinate heterogeneous representations, autonomous agents interact with external environments, and scientific generative systems propose candidate explanations, structures, and experiments. In these settings, a generation decision may influence not only the immediate output but also subsequent reasoning, tool execution, resource consumption, safety, and task completion. This paper proposes Lookahead Generative AI (LGAI), a unified research framework in which generative systems predict the potential downstream consequences of candidate actions before committing to a decision. The framework separates state representation, candidate-action generation, future-outcome prediction, cost-aware decision-making, execution, and outcome verification. It accommodates learned value functions, approximate rollouts, simulation, external evaluators, model ensembles, and other prediction mechanisms without requiring a single underlying model architecture. To support systematic implementation, the paper introduces a modular Research Slot Architecture and a catalogue of 300 candidate research directions spanning language generation, reasoning, agentic systems, software engineering, multimodal generation, scientific discovery, robotics, healthcare, education, business, security, model training, inference infrastructure, evaluation, and human–AI collaboration. Each direction specifies a potential application of predictive decision-making and can be developed as an independent implementation or experimental study. The catalogue is a research-development resource rather than a claim that all proposed directions are novel or effective. The principal scientific hypothesis is that explicit prediction of downstream consequences can improve decision quality when candidate actions have materially different future effects and when prediction costs are justified by the expected benefit. This hypothesis must be tested against fixed, greedy, heuristic, and learned non-lookahead baselines under controlled computational budgets.

title: Online Interval Selection with Binary Predictions: Optimal Consistency and a Continuous Robustness Tradeoff
abstract: We study online interval selection with binary predictions of membership in a final optimal solution. Requests arrive in arbitrary order; accepted requests may be revoked, but rejected or revoked requests cannot be recovered. With rewards proportional to interval length, the best consistency under finite strict robustness is $d=(3+\sqrt5)/2$ when both guarantees hold almost surely on each fixed input, including for randomized algorithms. A continuous lower bound forces consistency strictly above $d$ at every robustness budget below $4\varphi+3\approx9.472$, whereas our deterministic algorithm attains $d$ with exact robustness $\varphi^5\approx11.090$, where $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$. Each held interval inherits a ledger recording positive prediction mass lost through irrevocable decisions. A tunable replacement cost gives a continuous family with exact consistency throughout and exact robustness on two parameter intervals, including $(C,R)=(25/9,10)$ and $(4,7)$. Randomization permits expected consistency approaching one with finite expected robustness, whereas almost-sure robustness forces expected consistency strictly above two at every finite budget.

title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
abstract: Many everyday tasks require controlling contact force as well as motion. On a humanoid, this force must often be coordinated across both hands and the whole body, and cannot be specified by kinematic trajectories alone. Therefore, we present FLORE, a framework for learning force-reactive humanoid loco-manipulation. We collect robot-free demonstrations using two force-sensing UMI-style handheld grippers for hand motion and contact wrenches, and wearable trackers for body motion. A force-reactive diffusion policy takes vision, proprioception, and measured wrenches as input, then predicts actions and per-hand force commands. A hybrid compliance whole-body controller with force tracking executes these commands while maintaining balance: an integral of the force error measured by real force/torque (F/T) sensors lets each hand track force accurately along the commanded direction and remain compliant along the others. In simulation, the controller tracks per-hand force commands of varied magnitude and direction, with little loss in whole-body motion accuracy. Across three contact-rich tasks on the robot, the force-reactive policy succeeds in 80% of rollouts, compared with 26.7% for a position-only policy trained on the same demonstrations and executed by the same controller. For more details, please visit our website: https://louis-leee.github.io/FLoRe/.
